claim.title: Generated liveSwitch body hard-wires the 'live' input; standalone pipeline.run() (source=batch) diverges from canvas executor branch selection
claim.location: src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:521-539 (_gen_live_switch); src/haute/pipeline.py:327-362 (Pipeline.run sets _scenario_ctx='batch' and calls the literal body via Node.__call__ at pipeline.py:54-68); src/haute/_builders.py:633-666 (_build_live_switch routes by ctx.source)
claim.failure_scenario: A liveSwitch node maps input 'live_src'->scenario 'live' and 'batch_src'->scenario 'batch'. Codegen emits a body whose statement is `return live_src` (the scenario=='live' input, chosen at SAVE time). At runtime the executor's _build_live_switch selects the input whose scenario == ctx.source. For a non-live run (source='batch') the executor returns batch_src, but the generated standalone file ALWAYS returns live_src. Pipeline.run() forces _scenario_ctx='batch' AND invokes the literal generated body (there is no NODE_REGISTRY dispatch in Pipeline.run/score), so a standalone batch run of the saved file routes the LIVE frame while the in-canvas batch executor routes the BATCH frame — different rows/columns flow downstream with no error.
claim.repro_strategy: Build a GraphNode(LIVE_SWITCH, config={'input_scenario_map':{'live_src':'live','batch_src':'batch'}}); _gen_live_switch(node,['live_src','batch_src']) -> body contains `return live_src`. Compare _build_live_switch(ctx).fn(live_src=LIVE, batch_src=BATCH) under ctx.source='batch' -> returns BATCH. Confirmed: executor=BATCH, generated body=LIVE. Structural round-trip test (test_codegen_roundtrip_property.py:439-449) covers LIVE_SWITCH but only checks graph structure, not body runtime selection, so it does not catch this.

verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (claim reproduced). Under a batch run, the in-canvas executor and the standalone generated body route DIFFERENT input frames with no error. Key output lines: generated standalone body => `return live_src`; `executor (source='batch') routed branch = 'BATCH'`; `standalone Pipeline.run body (_scenario_ctx='batch') routed branch = 'LIVE'`. Final: in-canvas executor -> BATCH (correct), standalone saved file -> LIVE (wrong).
verdict.evidence: Three code paths confirmed both by trace and by execution. (1) Codegen: src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:268-273 `_LIVE_SWITCH` template body is `return {active_param}`, and :521-539 `_gen_live_switch` sets active_param = the input whose input_scenario_map value == 'live' (a SAVE-time constant). Repro emitted exactly `return live_src`. (2) Executor: src/haute/_builders.py:633-666 `_build_live_switch.switch_fn` selects the input whose scenario == ctx.source at RUNTIME; under source='batch' the repro got the BATCH frame. (3) Standalone run: src/haute/pipeline.py:195-197 `Pipeline.live_switch` -> `_register_node` (:103-128) stores the literal user fn as Node.fn (no scenario substitution); `Pipeline.run()` (:327-362) sets `_scenario_ctx.set('batch')` then calls `n(*input_dfs)` -> `Node.__call__` (:54-68) invokes `self.fn` (the literal `return live_src` body) with NO NODE_REGISTRY dispatch. Repro proved the literal body returns the LIVE frame even with `_scenario_ctx='batch'`. No guard exists: `_LIVE_SWITCH` is the sole codegen body template (grep showed no scenario-aware variant), and the cited round-trip test (tests/test_codegen_roundtrip_property.py `_roundtrip`) only checks generated-source structure/idempotency, never executing the body across scenarios — so it cannot catch this. Net: standalone batch run of the saved file routes the LIVE frame while the in-canvas batch executor routes the BATCH frame; different rows/columns flow downstream silently.
verdict.blast_radius: Any pipeline containing a liveSwitch node that is exported via codegen and then executed standalone through Pipeline.run() (source='batch'). The standalone file always routes the 'live'-mapped branch, so for batch/non-live runs it silently feeds the wrong upstream frame (different rows/columns) into everything downstream of the switch — producing wrong-but-plausible results with no error. The in-canvas executor is correct, so the divergence only manifests in the generated/exported artifact, making it easy to miss. Pipeline.score() forces source='live', so the live path happens to match the generated body; the corruption is specific to batch execution of the exported file.
verdict.recommended_fix: Make the generated liveSwitch body scenario-aware so it mirrors `_build_live_switch`. Change `_LIVE_SWITCH` (_codegen_builders.py:268-273) to emit a body that selects the input whose input_scenario_map value == the active source at runtime (e.g. read `haute._model_scorer._scenario_ctx.get()` / an equivalent source, default 'live'), rather than the hard-wired `return {active_param}`. The simplest robust option is to route through the same executor logic: have the generated body call a shared `select_live_switch_input(input_scenario_map, source, **frames)` helper used by both `_build_live_switch` and codegen, eliminating the duplicated branch-selection logic. Add an execution-level regression test that runs the generated standalone body under both `_scenario_ctx='live'` and `='batch'` and asserts the routed frame matches the executor (the existing round-trip property test is structural only and cannot catch this).
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. The fix touches central codegen/graph-model files (_codegen_builders.py, and ideally a shared helper in _builders.py). Current branch is `wave-2-cache-integrity` (theme: cache integrity), so direct overlap is unlikely, but these are hot files an in-flight codegen/executor feature could be editing. Keep the change localized to the live_switch template + one shared selection helper to minimize conflict surface.

claim.title: Generated optimiserApply body is a pure passthrough (return first); standalone pipeline.run() never applies the optimiser while the canvas executor does
claim.location: src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:405-410,847-854 (_OPTIMISER_APPLY passthrough template + _make_passthrough_builder); src/haute/codegen.py:304-345 (_optimiser_apply_ratebook_return_source returns None for sourceType in {run,registered} with unresolved mode, leaving `return {first}`); src/haute/_builders.py:969-1034,1375-1415 (_build_optimiser_apply + _select_optimiser_apply_input load the artifact and apply)
claim.failure_scenario: An optimiserApply node with sourceType='run', run_id set, ratebook_input pointing at the 2nd input, and optimiser_mode NOT yet 'ratebook'. Codegen emits `return data_src` (first input passthrough). At runtime the executor loads the MLflow artifact, and when artifact mode=='ratebook' applies the ratebook to dfs[source_ids.index(ratebook_input)] (the 2nd input) producing a version column + optimised values. The saved standalone file, run via pipeline.run(), executes the literal passthrough body — it never loads the artifact and never applies the optimiser at all (output equals the raw input frame). The canvas preview shows optimised prices; the deployed/standalone file emits un-optimised prices. More generally optimiser/modelling/scenarioExpander also emit `return {first}` bodies, so the operation never runs standalone, unlike banding/ratingStep/modelScore whose bodies call apply_*_from_config/score_from_config.
claim.repro_strategy: _node_to_code(optimiserApply node, ['data_src','ratebook_src'], ['data_node','rb_node']) with config sourceType='run', ratebook_input='rb_node' -> body `return data_src`. Separately build a Pipeline with @p.optimiser_apply(sourceType='run',run_id='abc',ratebook_input='rb') whose body is `return src`; p.run() output has only the input column (no __optimiser_version__) — confirmed passthrough. Contrast _select_optimiser_apply_input(dfs, {'mode':'ratebook'}, 'rb_node', names, ['data_node','rb_node']) -> dfs[1]. test_codegen_roundtrip_property.py:364-376 covers OPTIMISER_APPLY structurally only.

verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (all three parts confirm the bug). Part1: _node_to_code on the scenario node (sourceType='run', run_id='abc', ratebook_input='rb_node', optimiser_mode unset) emits body `return data_src` with NO artifact load / apply call. Part2: a Pipeline whose optimiserApply body is the generated `return src`, run via p.run(), yields output value-identical to the raw input with no __optimiser_version__ column => optimiser NOT applied standalone. Part3: _select_optimiser_apply_input(dfs,{'mode':'ratebook'},'rb_node',...) returns dfs[1] (the 2nd/ratebook input) — the input the standalone passthrough ignores. Supplemental one-liner: with optimiser_mode='ratebook' the rewrite path emits `return ratebook_src` — still a pure passthrough, still NO apply call, confirming the 'never applies standalone' property is universal, not scenario-specific.
verdict.evidence:
Generated standalone source for the scenario node (verbatim): `@pipeline.optimiser_apply(config="config/apply_optimisation/Apply_Optimiser.json", contract="opaque")
def Apply_Optimiser(data_src, ratebook_src) -> pl.LazyFrame:
    """apply"""
    return data_src`. Code-trace: (1) _codegen_builders.py:405-410 _OPTIMISER_APPLY body is literally `return {first}`, assigned via _make_passthrough_builder at 851-854. (2) codegen.py:319-324 _optimiser_apply_ratebook_return_source returns None for sourceType in {run,registered} with optimiser_mode!='ratebook', so _rewrite_single_return_source is skipped; and even when it runs (348-365) it only swaps WHICH input is returned, never inserts an apply call. (3) pipeline.py:103-128 _register_node stores the literal fn; Node.__call__ (54-68) and run() (339-352) call self.fn(...) directly — no config re-derivation for OPTIMISER_APPLY (cf. edge_join's special-cased _apply_edge_join). (4) _builders.py:969-1040 _build_optimiser_apply (reached via executor.py execute_graph -> _build_node_fn) loads the MLflow artifact and calls _dispatch_apply when _has_mlflow is true (sourceType='run'+run_id), producing __optimiser_version__ + optimised values. So canvas executor applies; standalone p.run() passes through. Contrast confirmed: _MODEL_SCORE/_BANDING/_RATING_STEP templates (_codegen_builders.py:275-369) emit bodies that call score_from_config/apply_banding_from_config/apply_rating_step_from_config, so those operations DO run standalone.
verdict.blast_radius: Every saved/deployed standalone pipeline file (run via pipeline.run()/score()) containing an optimiserApply node silently emits UN-optimised prices: the body is a pure input passthrough that never loads the artifact and never applies online/ratebook optimisation. The canvas preview (execute_graph -> _build_optimiser_apply) shows optimised prices, so preview and the saved file disagree — a silent correctness gap exactly where it matters (pricing output). The same defect affects optimiser, modelling, and scenarioExpander codegen bodies (all `return {first}`), so those node types also no-op in a standalone run, unlike banding/ratingStep/modelScore. Note: the separate deploy serving path (deploy/_scorer.py) DOES rebuild a real apply fn from config, so model serving is unaffected; the gap is the generated .py executed directly by pipeline.run()/score().
verdict.recommended_fix: Make the optimiserApply codegen body self-contained like banding/ratingStep/modelScore: emit a body that calls a config-driven helper (e.g. apply_optimiser_from_config(first, config=..., base_dir=base)) which loads the artifact (file or MLflow), selects the ratebook input via _select_optimiser_apply_input, and runs _dispatch_apply — mirroring _build_optimiser_apply / deploy/_scorer.py. The existing _rewrite_single_return_source ratebook-input wiring must feed that helper's input selection rather than just renaming the passthrough return. Apply the same fix to optimiser, modelling, and scenarioExpander templates (or confirm via an explicit standalone-execution test that a passthrough is the intended contract for those — currently only structural roundtrip is tested at test_codegen_roundtrip_property.py:364-376). Per repo TDD policy, first add a failing standalone-execution test asserting the generated file applies the optimiser (output gains __optimiser_version__ / optimised values).
verdict.coordinate_risk: Medium-high. The active branch is wave-2-cache-integrity and recent commits touch the rating optimiser (optimiser sources/regression CI). codegen.py optimiserApply wiring (_optimiser_apply_ratebook_return_source / _rewrite_single_return_source), _codegen_builders.py templates, and _builders.py optimiser apply are an actively-edited optimiser hot zone — coordinate with any in-flight optimiser/codegen work to avoid conflicting edits to the same template/builder functions.

claim.title: _format_contract_kwarg downgrades ANY non-ConfigError exception to contract="opaque", masking genuine contract-computation bugs and violating the fail-loud mandate
claim.location: src/haute/codegen.py:100-116 (_format_contract_kwarg broad `except Exception:` -> return 'contract="opaque"'); src/haute/_contracts.py:151-166 (get_column_contract dispatch)
claim.failure_scenario: The intent is to tolerate only MLflow/infra failures (unreachable server, missing artifact) when discovering MODEL_SCORE feature names. But the except clause catches Exception broadly. If the column-contract computation for any node type raises a genuine code defect (TypeError, KeyError, ContractMismatchError, AttributeError) — e.g. a malformed but non-ConfigError config, or a regression in a columns= callable — codegen silently emits contract="opaque" instead of the real input/output column set and logs only a warning. The saved file then carries no enforced contract for that node; the bug is hidden until far-away execution, and a wrong-but-plausible contract drift is never surfaced at save time. This directly contradicts CLAUDE.md's 'fail loudly, no incorrect fallbacks' mandate.
claim.repro_strategy: Monkeypatch haute.codegen.get_column_contract to raise TypeError('bug'); call _format_contract_kwarg(banding_node) -> returns 'contract="opaque"' with a warning log, no raise. Confirmed. A ConfigError correctly propagates, but every other exception class is swallowed.

verdict.evidence: Ran review/02-findings/repro/codegen__contract-emit-swallows-non-infra-bugs-to-opaque.py (exit 0). Observed: (1) baseline healthy banding node emits concrete contract={"inputs":['age'],"outputs":['age_band']}; (2) monkeypatched get_column_contract->raise TypeError: _format_contract_kwarg returned 'contract="opaque"' (no raise), log line "contract_emit_opaque_on_error ... error=\"...'int' object is not subscriptable\""; (3) raise ContractMismatchError (asserted NOT a ConfigError subclass) -> returned 'contract="opaque"'; (4) ConfigError control -> propagated (asymmetry confirmed); (5) NO-monkeypatch realistic case: malformed banding factors=["age"] (string not dict) makes the REAL registered _builders._banding_columns raise AttributeError "'str' object has no attribute 'get'", which _format_contract_kwarg swallows to 'contract="opaque"'. Code: src/haute/codegen.py:100-119 (except ConfigError: raise / except Exception: warn+return opaque sentinel; called live at codegen.py:408 and :512 then injected via _inject_contract_kwarg). src/haute/errors.py:70 ContractMismatchError(HauteError) is not a ConfigError. No compensating guard: parser.py has no opaque reconciliation; projection.overlay_declared_contract (projection.py:596-597) makes a saved opaque defer to the builder, and OpaqueContractRule (projection.py:1305+) relaxes boundary demands for opaque nodes -- so the save-time defect is never re-surfaced at save time.
verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (exit 0) — all four scenarios reproduced. TypeError, ContractMismatchError, and a real (un-patched) AttributeError from _banding_columns on a malformed factor are each downgraded to contract="opaque" with only a warning; ConfigError alone propagates, proving the catch is asymmetric and masks genuine contract-computation bugs at save time.
verdict.blast_radius: Affects every codegen/save of a pipeline whose node contract computation hits a non-ConfigError defect (any node type with a columns= callable: BANDING, RATING_STEP, MODEL_SCORE, CONSTANT, OPTIMISER_APPLY, SCENARIO_EXPANDER, etc.). Symptoms: the saved .py silently carries contract="opaque" instead of the real input/output column set, so the node's contract is no longer enforced and a wrong-but-plausible contract drift (ContractMismatchError) is never surfaced at save time. The bug only re-manifests far away at projection/execution (or stays hidden if execution takes a passthrough/opaque path), violating the fail-loud mandate. Not a data-corruption or crash bug — a silent loss of an integrity check — hence medium, not high.
verdict.recommended_fix: Narrow the rescue in _format_contract_kwarg (codegen.py:106) to the genuinely-infra exception types only. Since the docstring's stated intent is MLflow/infra tolerance, catch the specific MLflow/artifact failure classes (e.g. the exception raised by haute._mlflow_io.load_mlflow_model when the server is unreachable/artifact missing) and re-raise everything else — or, simplest, also re-raise HauteError (which covers ContractMismatchError/SchemaMismatchError/FeatureMismatchError) alongside ConfigError, and let TypeError/KeyError/AttributeError propagate as the code defects they are. Add a fail-loud test next to test_graph_to_code_refuses_to_emit_unparseable_file asserting that a contract fn raising TypeError/ContractMismatchError raises out of _format_contract_kwarg / graph_to_code rather than emitting contract="opaque". Keep the existing MLflow-down -> opaque path covered by a dedicated test so the narrowing does not regress the legitimate infra tolerance.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. codegen.py and the contract/projection pipeline are on the active wave-2-cache-integrity branch and recent commits touch rating-optimiser/projection regression tests, so this is a hot area an in-flight feature branch may be editing. The fix is localized to one except clause plus a new test in test_codegen_fail_loudly.py, but coordinate the exception-narrowing with anyone changing _builders contract callables or the MLflow load path to agree on which exception classes count as "infra".

claim.title: _format_contract_source guesses fan-in column ownership when exactly one stale parent and one unmatched parent exist, re-attributing columns to a possibly-wrong parent
claim.location: src/haute/codegen.py:135-176 (_format_contract_source single-stale/single-unmatched reassignment branch, lines 150-160); consumed by src/haute/projection.py:1784-1821 (declared_inputs_by_parent) and the EdgeJoin/POLARS fan-in narrowing rules
claim.failure_scenario: A node's contract carries inputs_by_parent keyed by a stale parent id (left behind after a UI rewire) owning column set C. The current graph has exactly one parent whose id/name is unclaimed by the emitted map. The heuristic assumes the stale metadata 'belongs' to that single unclaimed parent and re-attributes C to it. If the user actually rewired to a genuinely different upstream that owns a DIFFERENT column set, the emitted inputs_by_parent now mis-attributes C to NewParent. Projection's fan-in narrowing (declared_inputs_by_parent / EdgeJoinFanInRule) consumes this map to route per-parent column demand; a wrong attribution can prune a column the new parent genuinely needs (silent column drop) or demand a column it cannot produce. Projection's parent-set equality guard catches gross key mismatches but not a plausible single reassignment whose key still matches the lone unmatched parent.
claim.repro_strategy: _format_contract_source(Contract(inputs={'colX'},outputs={'out'},inputs_by_parent={'old_parent':{'colX'}}), parent_name_by_id={'p_new':'NewParent'}) -> emits inputs_by_parent={'NewParent':['colX']}. Confirmed the stale columns are silently reassigned to NewParent. Demonstrating an actual prune requires wiring this contract into a fan-in projection plan where NewParent's true contract omits colX.

verdict.repro_outcome: Exit 0, all assertions pass. PHASE 1: _format_contract_source(Contract(inputs={shared,good_col,only_good}, outputs={}, inputs_by_parent={'good_id':{shared,good_col}, 'old_parent':{shared,only_good}}), parent_name_by_id={'good_id':'Good','p_new':'NewParent'}) emits inputs_by_parent={'Good':['good_col','shared'],'NewParent':['only_good','shared']} -- the stale 'old_parent' columns are silently re-attributed to NewParent. PHASE 2: feeding that misattributed map into _compute_projection_plan on a 2-parent fan-in polars node yields edge_demands[('Good','join')]={'good_col','shared'} (only_good DROPPED from its true producer) and edge_demands[('NewParent','join')]={'only_good','shared'} (only_good wrongly demanded from a parent that does not produce it); no guard raised. Separately validated the real round-trip graph_to_code -> parse_pipeline_source: reparsed consumer has parent ids ['Good','NewParent'] and contract inputs_by_parent keyed by exactly those names (KEYS-MATCH-PARENT-IDS=True), so declared_inputs_by_parent's parent-set equality guard passes and the misattribution survives reload into projection.
verdict.evidence: codegen.py:150-160 single-stale/single-unmatched branch: when len(stale_inputs)==1 and len(unmatched_parent_names)==1 it does `inputs_by_parent[unmatched_parent_names[0]] = sorted(columns)` -- it assumes the stale metadata belongs to the lone unclaimed current parent and re-attributes the column set with no proof of ownership. The emitted map is keyed by parent NAME (unmatched_parent_names[0] is a value from parent_name_by_id.values()). I verified via real round-trip that generated code references parents by function name AND the reparsed graph's parent ids equal those names, so the keys match projection's parent_set. In projection.py declared_inputs_by_parent (1804-1816) only checks key-set equality (unknown/missing) -- it passes here because the lone unmatched parent name is a legitimate current parent id. PolarsFanInRule (1463-1522) then builds by_parent from the declared map: covered = union of all parent column sets, so `missing = base_contribution - covered` does NOT fire (only_good is still in the union, just under the wrong parent). Result: only_good is routed to NewParent and silently omitted from Good's edge demand. Confirmed by repro output line: "Good -> ['good_col', 'shared']" (only_good absent) and "NewParent -> ['only_good', 'shared']". The claim's conceded gap (parent-set equality guard catches gross mismatches but not a plausible single reassignment whose key still matches the lone unmatched parent) is exactly what the round-trip demonstrated.
verdict.blast_radius: Only fan-in (>=2 parent) nodes that (a) carry an explicit inputs_by_parent contract, (b) were saved/exported through graph_to_code after a UI rewire that left exactly one stale parent key while leaving exactly one current parent unclaimed, and (c) where the rewired-to parent owns a DIFFERENT column set than the stale parent. When it fires, projection silently drops the re-attributed column(s) from their true producer's edge (lossy projection -> later "column not found" at execution, or wrong/null results if the missing column is only read downstream) and over-demands them from a parent that cannot produce them. Single-parent topologies (the common rename/repair case the existing test test_graph_to_code_repairs_single_parent_stale_inputs_by_parent_key targets) are benign because the reassignment is to the same logical parent. The ambiguous (>1 stale or >1 unmatched) case is already handled safely by the else-branch that omits the metadata (lines 161-171). So the dangerous window is the narrow exactly-one/exactly-one multi-parent case.
verdict.recommended_fix: Do not guess ownership across a genuine rewire. The single-stale/single-unmatched reassignment (codegen.py:153-160) re-keys columns to a parent it has no evidence owns them. Safest: treat this case like the ambiguous one -- drop the stale inputs_by_parent and log contract_inputs_by_parent_omitted_stale, since edges + node body remain the source of truth and projection falls back to a correct (if wider) full-width boundary rather than a silently-wrong narrow one (consistent with the codebase's 'fail loud / no incorrect fallback' guidance in CLAUDE.md). If single-parent repair must be retained for the rename case, gate the reassignment so it only fires when the emitted map would have exactly ONE parent total (true single-parent topology), and omit the metadata whenever any other parent was already matched by id (i.e. a real fan-in). Add a regression test asserting that a 2-parent rewire where the new parent owns different columns omits inputs_by_parent instead of re-attributing.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. Current branch is wave-2-cache-integrity and recent commits touch projection/rating-optimiser regression CI; projection.py and codegen.py are both actively-evolving hot files in this fan-in/contract area, so an in-flight feature branch could be editing _format_contract_source or the fan-in rules. Coordinate any fix with whoever owns the contract/projection work to avoid conflicting edits in codegen.py:135-176 and projection.py:1427-1525/1784-1821.

claim.title: normalise_rating_key (Python mirror) and _rating_key_expr (Polars twin) disagree on non-integer Float32 values
claim.location: src/haute/_rating.py:309-343 (normalise_rating_key widens Float32->Float64 before Utf8 cast) vs 346-370 (_rating_key_expr casts the Float32 column directly); engine join uses the twin on both sides at _rating.py:583,596
claim.failure_scenario: For a Float32 column value 0.1, _rating_key_expr casts the Float32 column to Utf8 producing '0.1' (Polars formats f32 compactly). The Python mirror normalise_rating_key receives the value already widened to a Python float (the f64 image of the f32 bits = 0.10000000149011612) and formats it via a Float64 Utf8 cast -> '0.10000000149011612'. The two canonical forms differ. The engine's lookup join is internally consistent (both sides use the twin), and the normal sidecar flow authors entry keys as JSON f64 (clean '0.1'), so standard rating apply does NOT miss. The divergence becomes a real wrong-flag where the mirror is used independently of the twin: trace enrichment (_trace_enrichment) canonicalises observed factor cells with the mirror to decide matched/default, so for a Float32 factor column a row that the engine MATCHED can be shown as a MISS (or vice versa) in the actuary-facing waterfall; and any code path that builds a rating lookup from a true Float32 scalar key (not a JSON f64) would silently miss.
claim.repro_strategy: df=pl.DataFrame([pl.Series('k',[0.1],dtype=pl.Float32)]); df.select(_rating_key_expr('k',pl.Float32))['k'][0] == '0.1' while normalise_rating_key(df['k'].to_list()[0]) == '0.10000000149011612'. Confirmed mismatch for 0.1 and 1e20 under Float32; Float64 agrees. The realistic compact->expand sidecar round-trip yields '0.1' and matches Float32 data, so the standalone rating apply does not miss — the divergence bites the mirror-only trace path / direct-f32-keyed lookups.

verdict.evidence: Executed repro (exit 0, all assertions on exact wrong values). Key output lines: "(A) twin (f32 column cast) -> '0.1'" vs "(A) mirror (f64 image cast) -> '0.10000000149011612'" — the twin/mirror disagree. "(B) engine output value for f32 0.1 vs entry 0.1 -> 9.0" — the engine (twin on both join sides, _rating.py:583,596) genuinely MATCHES a Float32 0.1 column against an authored JSON-f64 entry key 0.1. "(C) jsonified input_row = {'score': 0.10000000149011612}" then "(C) no-default status='unmatched_value' matched=True matched_entry=None" — _enrich_single_table, fed the row exactly as the real trace pipeline produces it, cannot locate the engine-matched entry and emits a self-contradictory flag (claims matched yet shows no matching entry). "(C2) with-default status='default' matched=False default_used=True" — with a usable defaultValue equal to the real entry value, the divergence flips the flag to a hard wrong 'default'/matched=False even though the engine matched a real entry. Control "(control) Float64 0.1 status='matched'" proves the defect is specific to Float32 dtype erasure at the trace JSON boundary, not to the value 0.1. Data-flow verified: _rating.py:620 reverts the factor column to its original Float32 dtype, so the per-node eager output the trace correlator reads holds Float32; _trace_correlation._jsonify_row (line 86) routes the float through _json_safe.to_json_safe (line 49-50) which returns the finite float unchanged = the f64 image 0.10000000149011612; normalise_rating_key (_rating.py:339-342) then formats it via a Float64 Utf8 cast. The docstrings at _rating.py:330-333 and test_rating_key_agreement.py:24-26 DOCUMENT this Float32 exclusion but that is not a guard — no code prevents the wrong flag, and the two existing Float32 tests (lines 177,189) assert only the engine match, never enrichment agreement, so the path is unguarded and untested. Full suite tests/test_rating_key_agreement.py: 64 passed.
verdict.repro_outcome: Passed (exit 0): every predicted wrong value is asserted and confirmed. Twin='0.1', mirror='0.10000000149011612'; engine matches f32 0.1 to entry 0.1 (value 9.0); trace enrichment reports status='unmatched_value'/matched=True/matched_entry=None (no default) and status='default'/matched=False (default present) for the engine-MATCHED row; Float64 control reports 'matched'. Reproduced BECAUSE of the predicted twin/mirror divergence, not an unrelated setup/import error.
verdict.blast_radius: Engine pricing is unaffected (the lookup join is internally consistent — twin on both sides — so rates are correct). claim.title: mirror_cache_to_committed copytrees working/ -> committed/ without the per-dir build lock and uses bare rename (no Windows retry), unlike _swap_dir_into_place
claim.location: src/haute/_json_flatten.py:239-317 (no _build_lock_for; bare committed_dir.rename/tmp_dir.rename/backup.rename at 302/304/306/310) vs src/haute/_json_shred.py:302-312,905-938 (_rename_dir_with_retry)

If the preamble's `import utility` actually resolves (via sys.path / PYTHONPATH / an installed package / a parent dir on the path) to a module NOT among those two candidate dirs, editing the real module does not change any hashed candidate, so the fingerprint is unchanged and stale preview/trace DataFrames computed against the OLD utility code are served as fresh. Compounding: the AST detector only catches literal import/from-import/__import__/importlib.import_module/exec forms — an aliased re-export or a dynamically-constructed import name evades detection entirely (returns False), dropping utility from the key even when pipeline_dir IS correct. On SyntaxError it falls back to a naive substring 'utility' which can both over- and under-trigger.
claim.repro_strategy: Code-trace: a graph with source_file in dir P, preamble `import utility`, and the importable utility module living in a sys.path dir Q != P and != cwd. graph_fingerprint is invariant to edits of Q/utility.py because _utility_candidates_for_dir(P) only yields P/utility{.py,/} and cwd/utility{.py,/}. The executor binds the Q module at run time, so preview reflects old code while the key is unchanged.
claim.repro_notes: Design/scoping issue: the fingerprint's notion of 'which utility file' is heuristic (dir-scan) rather than tied to the import system's actual resolution, so it can diverge from the bytes the executor runs.

verdict.repro_outcome: Exit 0, both blocks reproduced. Block A: preamble_execution_fingerprint("import utility", pipeline_dir=P) == af9bb475943a11b4 BEFORE and af9bb475943a11b4 AFTER editing the utility.py that `import utility` actually resolves to (verified via real importlib.import_module: scale(10) went 10 -> 1000). The module lived in a third sys.path dir Q != pipeline_dir, != cwd, while P/utility and cwd/utility were absent on disk, so the dir-scan candidates were both "missing" and the digest never moved. Block B: preamble_imports_utility("import utility")=True but the dynamically-built name importlib.import_module('util'+'ity') returns False, dropping utility content from the key even when pipeline_dir is correct and a utility.py is present.
verdict.evidence: Code-trace corroborates the runtime half: src/haute/executor.py:269-280 _prioritise_preamble_import_paths only MOVES cwd and pipeline_dir to the front of sys.path (sys.path[:] = [e for e in sys.path if e != path]; sys.path.insert(0, path)); it never removes other entries, so a utility module on a pre-existing sys.path dir Q stays resolvable when neither cwd nor pipeline_dir shadows it. _exec_preamble_namespace (executor.py:296-300) then exec()s the preamble, binding Q's `utility` into the namespace -> preview/trace reflect Q's bytes. Meanwhile graph_fingerprint -> preamble_execution_fingerprint (src/haute/_cache.py:371-397) hashes only _utility_candidates_for_dir(pipeline_dir) (_cache.py:302-317), which yields exactly {pipeline_dir,cwd}/utility{.py,/} -> both missing -> {"kind":"missing"} -> digest invariant to edits of Q. The fingerprint's notion of "which utility file" is a dir-scan heuristic that diverges from the import system's actual resolution. Verified no guard prevents this: there is no check that the resolved `utility.__file__` is among the hashed candidates, and _evict_utility_import_state (executor.py:249-266) likewise only evicts pyc for the same dir-scan candidates (so even cache-miss eviction is scoped to P/cwd, not Q). The repro asserted on the specific wrong VALUE (identical hash vs changed imported behaviour), not merely on an exception.
verdict.blast_radius: Preview and trace caches (graph_fingerprint feeds both via trace.py and executor.py) plus the _compile_preamble lru_cache, whose execution_fingerprint is the same value. Any pipeline whose preamble does `import utility` / `from utility …` where the utility module is resolved from a sys.path/PYTHONPATH/installed/editable-install/parent-dir location that is NOT cwd and NOT the pipeline file's immediate parent, AND where neither of those two dirs contains a shadowing utility module. In that layout, edits to the real utility code are silently NOT reflected: stale preview/trace DataFrames and a stale compiled preamble namespace are served as fresh until something else changes the key (e.g. preamble text, pipeline structure, or process restart). Secondary, layout-independent path: any preamble that imports utility via a dynamically-constructed / aliased name evades the AST detector and drops utility content from the key entirely even when pipeline_dir is correct. Not the default single-folder layout, but plausible for repos where pipelines live in nested subfolders (e.g. rating/<sub>/) while utility/ sits at a repo root that is on the path but is neither cwd nor the pipeline's parent.
verdict.recommended_fix: Tie the utility-content hash to the import system's ACTUAL resolution rather than a two-dir scan. After determining imports_utility, resolve the spec without executing (importlib.util.find_spec("utility") under the same prioritised sys.path used at exec time) and hash spec.origin / spec.submodule_search_locations; mix that resolved path set into the fingerprint (and use the same set for _evict_utility_import_state). This makes the key track exactly the bytes the executor binds, regardless of which sys.path dir wins. For the AST detector, accept that dynamic/aliased import names cannot be statically proven: when the preamble contains importlib.import_module / __import__ / exec with a non-constant first arg (or any import machinery the walker cannot resolve to a literal), conservatively treat utility as possibly-imported (or, better, drive inclusion off the post-exec resolved-modules set rather than pre-exec AST). Reconsider the SyntaxError substring fallback ("utility" in preamble) once resolution is spec-based.
verdict.coordinate_risk: High. The current branch is wave-2-cache-integrity and the most recent commit touching this code is 57153a92 "W2.2+2.3 (C4): preview and trace keys sign every file-backed input" — i.e. an in-flight effort whose stated goal is to sign every file-backed input into the preview/trace keys, but which scopes "file-backed input" to the dir-scan candidates and thus leaves this sys.path gap open. src/haute/_cache.py and src/haute/executor.py are the hot files for this wave, so any fix must be coordinated with that in-flight work (and ideally bundled as a follow-up to the same C4 item) to avoid conflicting edits to _utility_candidates_for_dir / preamble_execution_fingerprint / _prioritise_preamble_import_paths.

claim.title: store_artifact calls self.get(key) after put, re-validating (scan_parquet) the just-written artifact under the lock; a transient parquet read failure raises CacheArtifactCorrupt and evicts a valid store
claim.location: src/haute/_dataframe_execution_cache.py:487-495 (evict_where + put + self.get(key) -> _evict_if_invalid -> _validate_entry) and 393-415, 542-556
claim.failure_scenario: store_artifact, after put, calls self.get(key) which runs _evict_if_invalid -> _validate_entry -> pl.scan_parquet(entry.path).collect_schema(). If that read transiently fails (Windows sharing violation against the file just written, antivirus lock, slow flush), _validate_entry raises CacheArtifactCorruptError, _evict_if_invalid catches it, calls _remove_key (unlinking the artifact since it has no live scans), and get returns None, so store_artifact raises DataFrameExecutionCacheError('Stored dataframe cache entry vanished immediately'). A perfectly valid just-materialised frame is deleted and the execution fails loudly on a transient read, rather than retrying. The same revalidation-on-store happens again in materialize_lazy_frame_with_cache via scan(key) at 615. This couples store success to an immediate second open of the same file.
claim.repro_strategy: Standalone: monkeypatch pl.scan_parquet (or DataFrameExecutionCache._validate_entry) to raise once on the just-stored path, then call store_artifact; assert it raises 'vanished immediately' and the artifact was unlinked, despite the write having succeeded.
claim.repro_notes: On the documented Windows target the just-written-then-immediately-reopened file is exactly where sharing violations appear; the design treats any open failure as permanent corruption with no retry, unlike the rename path which retries PermissionError.

verdict.evidence: Code-trace + executed repro both confirm the mechanism. store_artifact (src/haute/_dataframe_execution_cache.py:487-495) does `self.put(...)` then `stored = self.get(key)`; if `stored is None` it raises DataFrameExecutionCacheError("...vanished immediately"). get() (360-367) unconditionally calls `_evict_if_invalid(entry)` (365), which calls `_validate_entry` (404) -> `pl.scan_parquet(entry.path).collect_schema()` (550). `_validate_entry`'s `except Exception` (551) wraps ANY read error (incl. a Windows PermissionError/sharing violation on the just-written file) as CacheArtifactCorruptError. `_evict_if_invalid` catches it (406) and calls `_remove_key` (414). The override `_remove_key` (527-540) unlinks the file when `not had_live_scans`, where `had_live_scans = super()._is_pinned(key)` — and the base `_is_pinned` (lru_cache.py:273-274) checks only the scan-pin/`_pin_slots` sets, NOT `_store_pins`. A just-stored entry is never scan-pinned (pin() is only called in scan() at 378), so the store-window `_store_pins` protection (which only guards eviction-VICTIM selection via the `_is_pinned` override at 512-515) does NOT prevent this unlink. Repro output: "store_artifact raised 'vanished immediately' on a single transient revalidation read -> valid just-written artifact was UNLINKED (data destroyed) -> a subsequent identical store succeeded (failure was transient); _validate_entry call count during store: 1", plus the real warning log `dataframe_execution_cache_invalid_entry_evicted`. There is NO try/except/retry around the `self.get(key)` call. The same revalidation path also exists at materialize_lazy_frame_with_cache scan(key) line 615 (scan() also calls _evict_if_invalid at 374). NOTE: the claim's secondary aside that "the rename path retries PermissionError" is inaccurate — atomic_write (_polars_utils.py:286-293) propagates PermissionError without retry and _collect_lazy_frame only retries Polars compute errors — but that detail is not load-bearing for the core finding, which holds.
verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (bug reproduced). Injected exactly one transient CacheArtifactCorruptError into _validate_entry for the just-stored, genuinely-valid parquet. store_artifact raised DataFrameExecutionCacheError containing "vanished immediately"; the valid artifact file was unlinked (artifact.exists() == False); cache.get(key) became None; a subsequent non-flaky store of identical data succeeded, proving the destroyed data was recoverable and the failure transient. All assertions on specific expected-vs-actual values passed. Isolated under tempfile.TemporaryDirectory; no src/, tests/, or rating/ files read or written.
verdict.blast_radius: Any cache-backed lazy execution on the documented Windows target (materialize_lazy_frame_with_cache -> store_artifact, and again via scan(key) at line 615). Trigger is a transient read failure (sharing violation / AV lock / slow flush) on the just-written parquet in the write-then-immediately-reopen window. When it fires: the just-materialised frame is deleted and the whole execution fails loudly with "vanished immediately" instead of using the frame it just wrote. Not a silent corruption or persistent leak — the entry is treated as a miss, so a rerun self-heals (no orphaned files: the file is unlinked, not leaked). Impact is a spurious hard run-failure that discards recoverable work; frequency is environment-dependent (rare-to-occasional on Windows under AV, ~never on Linux).
verdict.recommended_fix: Decouple store-success from an immediate second open of the just-written file. Two clean options: (a) In store_artifact, after put(), do not route the existence check through self.get()/_evict_if_invalid — fetch the entry without revalidating (the artifact was just written and its metadata just read by read_parquet_metadata), e.g. a lock-held `super().get(key.cache_key)` presence check, so a transient reopen cannot evict a freshly-stored entry; or (b) make _validate_entry / _evict_if_invalid distinguish a transient open failure (e.g. Windows PermissionError / sharing-violation OSError) from genuine parquet corruption and retry the open a few times with a short backoff (mirroring how I/O contention is handled elsewhere) before declaring the artifact corrupt and unlinking it. Option (a) is the smaller, more targeted change and removes the redundant reopen entirely. Add a regression test asserting that one transient revalidation failure does not unlink a valid just-stored artifact nor raise "vanished immediately".
verdict.coordinate_risk: Medium. _dataframe_execution_cache.py is the focus of the current branch (wave-2-cache-integrity) and recent commits touch cache integrity; the store-window/_store_pins and _evict_if_invalid logic is exactly the hot area an in-flight cache-integrity feature is likely editing. Any fix should be coordinated with that branch's changes to materialization_lock / store-window semantics to avoid conflicts.

claim.title: Scalar-array child tables always name their column 'value' with a $value leaf; a single-port apiInput returns a bare LazyFrame, so a scalar port and an object port with a real 'value' field are indistinguishable to consumers
claim.location: src/haute/_json_shred.py:72-73 (_SCALAR_VALUE_LEAF/_SCALAR_VALUE_COLUMN), 509-536 (_resolve_leaf $value handling), 1027-1031 (single-port bare-LazyFrame shorthand in load_v2_api_source)
claim.failure_scenario: A scalar-array table materialises a single column literally named 'value' (from the reserved $value leaf), while an object table can legitimately have a user column also named 'value'. load_v2_api_source returns a bare LazyFrame for a single emitting port (no label/kind metadata), and the per-frame footer records port_label but consumers of the bare frame see only a column called 'value'. Downstream wiring that distinguishes scalar-port vs object-port semantics by column shape can misread one for the other; and because the scalar column name is fixed, two different conceptual scalar arrays both surface as a column named 'value', so a port-handle/source-handle rewire that swaps which scalar array feeds a consumer is invisible at the column-name layer (only the table label/path, which IS in the fingerprint, distinguishes them).
claim.repro_strategy: Code-trace: infer a schema for data with both a scalar array (-> column 'value') and an object table containing a field named 'value'; observe both produce a column named 'value'. Confirm load_v2_api_source single-port path returns a bare LazyFrame carrying no scalar-vs-object discriminator beyond the column name.
claim.repro_notes: Lower severity because table label/path are fingerprinted (so cache identity is safe) and B2 prevents filename collisions; the risk is downstream consumer ambiguity, not a direct cache mis-hit.

verdict.evidence:
The claim's factual premises are accurate but its operative failure ("indistinguishable to consumers" / "can misread one for the other") is refuted by the actual routing code.

VERIFIED-TRUE premises:
- _json_shred.py:1200-1208 hardcodes scalar-table column name to _SCALAR_VALUE_COLUMN="value" (defined :72-73) with reserved $value leaf.
- :1211-1220 an object table's column name is the raw JSON key, so a JSON field literally named "value" yields a column "value"; validate_v2_schema (_api_input_schema.py:263-389) never forbids a user column named "value". So both DO surface a column literally named "value".
- load_v2_api_source :1028-1029 returns a bare LazyFrame for a single emitting port; the per-frame footer records port_label (:739) but the runtime return is just bundle[label] (a LazyFrame), so the consumer sees only columns.

WHY THE CONSEQUENCE IS REFUTED:
- The executor resolves which port frame feeds a consumer STRICTLY by edge.sourceHandle, never by column shape: _execute_lazy.py:_pick_source_frame :64-117 — for a dict source it picks source_output[edge.sourceHandle] (raises ValueError/KeyError on missing/unknown handle); for a bare frame (single-port) it passes through and IGNORES sourceHandle (:117). Function-parameter binding is keyed by `edge.sourceHandle or edge.source` (:931, MULTI_FRAME_PLAN §4b). No "downstream wiring that distinguishes scalar-port vs object-port by column shape" exists.
- A full scan for any consumer branching on the literal "value" column for apiInput port semantics found none: the "value" literals in src (Grep) are all unrelated subsystems (rating lookup _rating.py, banding, charts, metrics, _json_safe). _rating.py:574-576 even renames its own "value" to an internal name to avoid input collisions — a guard, in a different subsystem. The shred-time shape guard at _json_shred.py:629-630 discriminates scalar-vs-object using the unambiguous $value LEAF in col_specs, NOT the "value" column name, and is internal to the shred (not exposed downstream). No frontend source distinguishes ports by "value"/"$value" either (Grep over ts/tsx/vue/svelte: none).
- "Indistinguishable to consumers" is also overstated: a scalar port is a single-column [value] frame; an object port with a real "value" field plus any other field is a multi-column frame, trivially distinguishable; only the degenerate single-column object table named "value" would coincide, and even then nothing routes by shape.

CACHE IDENTITY (claim concedes safe; confirmed): _v2_fingerprint :136-143 hashes table path+label AND per-column path. The scalar leaf path is "$[*].coverages[*].$value" vs a real field "$[*].drivers[*].value" — different paths in the fingerprint. A port/source-handle rewire changes edge.sourceHandle (the routing key), and tables are distinguished by fingerprinted path/label. So no cache mis-hit and no silent rewire.

Net: factual premises true; predicted failure (consumer misread) has no realization path in the codebase. testable:false, so no repro written — there is no wrong VALUE to assert on; the verification is a control/data-flow trace.
verdict.repro_outcome: No repro written: claim is testable:false and the predicted failure has no code path to exercise. Verification is a code-trace. The single discriminator that the claim says is missing (port identity) is in fact carried by edge.sourceHandle/label end-to-end, and the fingerprint distinguishes the scalar $value leaf-path from a real "value" field-path.

claim.title: Byte-budget chunk sizing estimates target row width from SOURCE schema only, so downstream-created wide/string columns fall back to 64 bytes and the target chunk can exceed the memory budget
claim.location: src/haute/chunking.py:607-626 (_plan_chunk_sizes target_row_bytes), 629-651 (_estimate_projected_row_bytes), 654-692 (_source_projected_column_widths)
claim.failure_scenario: A byte-budget chunk plan (target_chunk_bytes set, chunk_size=None) over a graph whose chunk suffix CREATES columns the source does not have: e.g. dataSource(parquet, a few narrow numeric cols) -> modelScore(prediction) or scenarioExpander or a polars with_columns that builds a wide String column (e.g. concat_str of several fields) feeding the target. _plan_chunk_sizes computes target_row_bytes = _estimate_projected_row_bytes(target_columns, source_node=<the dataSource>). _source_projected_column_widths returns {} for every column NOT present in the source schema, and _estimate_projected_row_bytes then assigns _DEFAULT_PROJECTED_COLUMN_BYTES (64) per such column. A produced String column averaging, say, 2KB/row is costed at 64 bytes — a 30x under-estimate. chunk_size = target_chunk_bytes // target_row_bytes is therefore ~30x too large, and the materialized target chunk (streaming_collect at chunking.py:1029) holds ~30x the intended bytes, breaking the bounded-memory contract the chunked path promises and the admission budget assumes.
claim.repro_strategy: Build a 2-node graph: dataSource(parquet with one Int64 col 'id', say 100k rows) -> polars node with code `df = df.with_columns(pl.concat_str([pl.col('id'), pl.lit('x'*2000)]).alias('big'))` (row-local, whitelisted). chunk_plan(ChunkPlanRequest(graph, target=polars_node, target_chunk_bytes=1_000_000)). Assert plan.estimated_target_row_bytes is ~64 (proving the source-only estimate ignores 'big'), then iter_chunked_frames and measure batch.frame.estimated_size() of the first chunk — it will be ~chunk_size*2KB >> 1MB target_chunk_bytes. Minimal: even assert plan.chunk_size computed against the under-estimate vs a real per-row width.

verdict.evidence: Executed repro output: `estimated_target_row_bytes = 72` (= 8 for Int64 `id` from source + 64 fallback for the downstream-created String column `big`), while the REAL per-row width of `big` is ~2004 B and the real full row ~2012 B -> a 27.9x under-count. The plan chose `chunk_size = 13888`, so the materialized target chunk projects to ~27.9 MB against the stated `target_chunk_bytes = 1_000_000` (1 MB) budget — a ~28x overshoot. Code-trace confirms the mechanism with no downstream guard: chunking.py:608 `target_columns = projection.needed_by_node.get(request.target_node_id)` returns {id, big}; chunking.py:609-613 calls `_estimate_projected_row_bytes(target_columns, source_node=<dataSource>)`; `_source_projected_column_widths` (654-659) only inspects the dataSource schema and returns {} for any column not in it, so 648-651 assigns `_DEFAULT_PROJECTED_COLUMN_BYTES = 64` (chunking.py:180) to `big`. projection.py:1149 (`demand = (demand - outputs) | refs`) proves the derived `big` is NOT propagated to the source demand, so it can never appear in the source schema width map. The runner at chunking.py:1029 does `streaming_collect(target_lf, ...)` fully materializing the oversized chunk into the yielded `pl.DataFrame` with no byte cap or re-costing. The pre-existing test `test_byte_budgeted_chunk_plan_shrinks_wide_projected_schema` (tests/test_chunk_plan.py:156) only exercises wide columns that exist IN the source, so this downstream-created case is untested.
verdict.repro_outcome: EXIT=0 (bug reproduced). Key lines: `estimated_target_row_bytes = 72`; `chunk_size = 13888`; `REAL big per-row bytes = 2004`; `under-count factor = 27.9x`; `projected chunk bytes = 27938892 (budget 1000000)`. All four assertions (estimate == id8 + fallback64; produced col > 1500 B; under-count > 20x; projected chunk > 20x budget) held, confirming the source-only estimate ignores the suffix-created `big` and the byte-budget chunk_size blows the memory budget ~28x.
verdict.blast_radius: Affects only the byte-budget chunk path (target_chunk_bytes set, chunk_size=None) AND only when the chunk suffix CREATES columns the single dataSource root lacks — e.g. a row-local polars with_columns/concat_str producing a wide String column, or modelScore/scenarioExpander adding wide outputs. Each such produced column is costed at 64 B regardless of true width, so chunk_size is inflated proportionally and the materialized target DataFrame held in memory per chunk (chunking.py:1029-1047) exceeds the stated budget by the same factor (~28x for a 2 KB String column). Breaks the bounded-memory contract the chunked path promises and that any memory-admission budget keyed off target_chunk_bytes assumes; risk of OOM on large row counts. The explicit-chunk_size path and byte-budget plans whose suffix only narrows/passes through source columns are unaffected.
verdict.recommended_fix: Cost the target row width from the TARGET node's actual output schema, not the source schema. Options: (a) derive a projected output schema by lazily building the chunk suffix (collect_schema on the target lazyframe restricted to needed_by_node[target]) and map dtypes via _dtype_estimated_width, sampling String/variable-width columns the same way _source_projected_column_widths samples the source; or (b) if a produced column's width cannot be proven (no concrete dtype/sample available), fail loud with ChunkPlanUnsupportedError rather than silently applying the 64 B default — consistent with the module's fail-loud stance and the project rule against silent fallbacks. A regression test mirroring the repro (downstream-created wide String column, assert estimated_target_row_bytes reflects ~2 KB and chunk_size keeps projected chunk bytes <= target_chunk_bytes) should pin it.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Yes — this sits squarely in the execution-engine chunking subsystem (src/haute/chunking.py _plan_chunk_sizes / _estimate_projected_row_bytes / _source_projected_column_widths) and the work is on branch `wave-2-cache-integrity`. The byte-budget sizing and projection-demand interaction is a hot area an in-flight chunking/cache-integrity feature branch may be editing; coordinate to avoid conflicting edits to the projected-row-width estimation and its tests in tests/test_chunk_plan.py.

claim.title: streaming_collect/bounded_collect_batches silently override the explicitly-passed profile with any ambient ExecutionContext on the contextvar, so allow_broad gating and bounded-memory semantics follow the wrong profile under nested execution
claim.location: src/haute/_polars_utils.py:65-71 (streaming_collect profile resolution + allow_broad check), 115-119 (bounded_collect_batches)
claim.failure_scenario: streaming_collect computes `metrics_context = execution_context or current_execution_context()` then `normalised_profile = metrics_context.profile if metrics_context is not None else _normalise_profile(profile)`. The explicitly-passed `profile=` argument is therefore IGNORED whenever ANY ExecutionContext is active on the contextvar (set by every ExecutionContext.stage()). The allow_broad validation at line 70 (`if allow_broad and normalised_profile not in _BROAD_COLLECT_PROFILES`) and the bounded-vs-broad decision at line 79 then use the contextvar profile, not the caller's. Concretely: a preview (PREVIEW_EAGER context active, allow_broad=True for the diamond multi-port collect at _execute_lazy.py:1878) that internally triggers any helper which calls streaming_collect with a bounded profile (e.g. CHUNKED_MAP_REDUCE or LAZY_SINK) will instead run as PREVIEW_EAGER and may broaden to a full .collect() (line 92) where the caller intended a fail-loud bounded collect. The reverse — a chunk/sink helper called while a PREVIEW_EAGER stage is on the contextvar of the same thread — would inherit PREVIEW_EAGER and bypass the BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError the bounded contract relies on.
claim.repro_strategy: Construct an ExecutionContext(profile=PREVIEW_EAGER); enter ctx.stage('x'); inside, call streaming_collect(lf_that_is_streaming_incompatible, profile=ExecutionProfile.LAZY_SINK, allow_broad=False) with NO execution_context kwarg. Expected (per LAZY_SINK bounded contract): BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError. Observed: the call resolves profile=PREVIEW_EAGER from the contextvar; because allow_broad defaults False it still raises, but flip allow_broad logic by asserting that streaming_collect(..., profile=LAZY_SINK, allow_broad=True) is ACCEPTED (no ValueError) while the same call with no active context RAISES ValueError('allow_broad=True is not permitted for profile lazy_sink'). The divergence proves the explicit profile is overridden.

verdict.repro_outcome: Exit 0. The repro confirms the OVERRIDE MECHANISM is real: identical call `streaming_collect(lf, profile=LAZY_SINK, allow_broad=True)` raises `ValueError("allow_broad=True is not permitted for profile 'lazy_sink'")` with no ambient context (Case A), but is ACCEPTED when a PREVIEW_EAGER ExecutionContext is active via ctx.stage (Case B); the recorded stage metric carries profile='preview_eager' n_collects=1, proving the explicit LAZY_SINK was replaced by the ambient profile. HOWEVER a second executed check refutes the claimed HARM: under an ambient PREVIEW_EAGER stage, `streaming_collect(fake_lf, profile=LAZY_SINK, allow_broad=False)` whose streaming collect raises a 'stream' compat error STILL raises BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError (output: "bounded fail-loud preserved -> BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError; profile in payload = Bounded streaming collect failed (profile=preview_eager, cause=ComputeError)") and the broad .collect() guard (AssertionError) never fired. The bounded contract is preserved; only the profile LABEL in the payload is wrong.
verdict.evidence: Mechanism is real (src/haute/_polars_utils.py:65-68): `metrics_context = execution_context or current_execution_context()`; `normalised_profile = metrics_context.profile if metrics_context is not None else _normalise_profile(profile)`. ExecutionContext.stage() publishes self on the contextvar (_execution_context.py:746 `_CURRENT_EXECUTION_CONTEXT.set(self)`), and the preview eager loop runs inside such a stage (executor.py:1038 `with _execution_stage(execution_context, "preview_cache_miss")` wrapping `_eager_execute`). So nested bounded collects without execution_context= inherit the ambient profile. BUT the claimed consequences are refuted by two guards the finder missed: (1) The allow_broad gate (line 70) and broadening to full .collect() (lines 85-92) are BOTH gated on allow_broad=True. The override does NOT flip allow_broad. Bounded callers pass allow_broad=False (default), and line 79 `if not allow_broad: raise BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError(...)` fires INDEPENDENT of profile — so a bounded collect can never silently broaden, regardless of the ambient profile. Confirmed empirically (broad .collect() never invoked). (2) The only three allow_broad-capable call sites — _execute_lazy.py:1878 (the claim's named locus), :1996, :2003 — themselves derive the profile from execution_context.profile (lines 1869-1874, 1987-1992: `collect_profile = execution_context.profile if execution_context is not None else PREVIEW_EAGER; allow_broad = collect_profile == PREVIEW_EAGER`). Thus the explicit profile they pass ALWAYS equals what streaming_collect re-resolves from the contextvar (or both are None) — zero divergence.
