claim.title: RustyStats/pyfunc models logged with loader_module='haute._mlflow_io' that exposes no _load_pyfunc/load_model entry point
claim.location: src/haute/modelling/_mlflow_log.py:471-476; src/haute/_mlflow_io.py:444-447 (only _load_pyfunc_model(mlflow, run_id, artifact_path) exists)
claim.failure_scenario: For non-CatBoost models (.rsglm GLM, and the generic branch), _log_model_with_signature calls mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(loader_module='haute._mlflow_io', ...). MLflow's pyfunc loader-module contract requires the named module to define a module-level _load_pyfunc(path) (or load_model) callable. haute._mlflow_io defines only _load_pyfunc_model(mlflow_module, run_id, artifact_path) — a different name and signature. Any consumer that loads the advertised flavor via mlflow.pyfunc.load_model('runs:/<run>/model') hits an AttributeError / loader-contract failure. haute itself never trips this because run discovery (_find_rsglm_artifact) finds the separately-logged native .rsglm and loads that; the advertised pyfunc flavor (and its attached ModelSignature, the documented deploy drift surface) is non-functional for external/standard MLflow tooling.
claim.repro_strategy: Log a fake .rsglm via _log_model_with_signature (or train a GLM with MLflow logging), then call mlflow.pyfunc.load_model(f'runs:/{run_id}/model') and observe the loader-module error. Or statically assert that haute._mlflow_io has no module-level attribute named _load_pyfunc or load_model.

verdict.evidence:
Executed repro at review/02-findings/repro/modelling__pyfunc-loader-module-missing-symbol.py reproduces the bug end-to-end.

STATIC: `haute._mlflow_io._load_pyfunc present : False`, `load_model present : False`, but `_load_pyfunc_model : True`. The module only defines `_load_pyfunc_model(mlflow_module, run_id, artifact_path)` (src/haute/_mlflow_io.py:444) — wrong name and wrong signature for the MLflow loader-module contract.

DYNAMIC: After logging a fake `.rsglm` through the REAL `_log_model_with_signature` (src/haute/modelling/_mlflow_log.py:471-476, non-CatBoost branch):
  `[dynamic] advertised loader_module = 'haute._mlflow_io'`
  `[dynamic] signature attached       = True`
  `[dynamic] load_model raised        = AttributeError: module 'haute._mlflow_io' has no attribute '_load_pyfunc'`
The AttributeError is NOT an import failure (haute imports fine) — it is exactly the predicted missing-symbol failure.

CONTRACT CONFIRMED in MLflow 3.10.0 source: .venv/.../mlflow/pyfunc/__init__.py:1168-1170 does `importlib.import_module(conf[MAIN])._load_pyfunc(data_path[, model_config])`, where conf[MAIN] is the logged `loader_module`. So MLflow calls `haute._mlflow_io._load_pyfunc(...)`, which does not exist.

WHY HAUTE DOESN'T TRIP IT (claim's secondary assertion verified): `_log_model_with_signature` also logs the native `.rsglm` separately (_mlflow_log.py:476). On load, `_find_model_artifact` (_mlflow_io.py:532-552) returns flavor "rustystats" for the `.rsglm` BEFORE the pyfunc fallback (556-570); `load_mlflow_model` (_mlflow_io.py:1015) then routes flavor in ("catboost","rustystats") to `_load_with_bounded_retry`, and only the else-branch (1025) calls `_load_pyfunc_model`. So haute's own scoring never loads the advertised pyfunc flavor.

PRODUCER CONFIRMED REAL: _training_job.py:36 maps "glm" -> ".rsglm"; every trained model with a model_path routes through _log_model_with_signature (_mlflow_log.py:217-229), so real GLM runs advertise this broken flavor. The "generic" branch is also affected but currently has no producer (only catboost/glm in _MODEL_EXT_MAP). The deploy serving path (deploy/_mlflow.py:124) uses python_model=_MODEL_CODE_PATH, not loader_module, so production serving is unaffected.
verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (claim confirmed). Script exits 0 with "[exit] repro completed: claim REAL." Static assertions confirm no _load_pyfunc/load_model symbol exists; dynamic assertion confirms mlflow.pyfunc.load_model('runs:/<run>/model') raises AttributeError: module 'haute._mlflow_io' has no attribute '_load_pyfunc', and that this is the missing-symbol failure (not an unrelated import/setup error). One earlier run failed on a test-fixture dtype typo (float64 vs Float64), which I fixed; that was my harness, not the bug.
verdict.blast_radius: Affects every non-CatBoost trained model logged with MLflow (real .rsglm GLM runs; the generic branch has no current producer). The advertised python_function flavor and its attached ModelSignature — the documented deploy drift-detection surface (mlflow.models.get_model_info(uri).signature) is still readable, but the flavor cannot be instantiated — are non-functional for ANY standard MLflow consumer doing mlflow.pyfunc.load_model('runs:/<run>/model') or 'models:/...'. Haute's own training/scoring is unaffected (loads the separately-logged native .rsglm). Production Databricks serving via deploy/_mlflow.py is unaffected (it uses python_model, not loader_module). Impact is therefore: external/standard MLflow tooling, model registry consumers, and anyone treating the pyfunc flavor as the canonical loadable artifact — they get a broken model. Silent because haute's CI/scoring never exercises the pyfunc load of these runs.
verdict.recommended_fix: Make the advertised loader module honor MLflow's contract. Cleanest: stop logging non-CatBoost models via a bare loader_module pointing at a module that has no _load_pyfunc; instead log them through a proper pyfunc PythonModel (mirroring deploy/_mlflow.py which passes python_model=...), OR add a module-level def _load_pyfunc(path) in haute._mlflow_io that loads the native model from `path` (e.g. dispatch on suffix to _load_rustystats_model / load_local_model) and returns a pyfunc-compatible wrapper, AND pass data_path so MLflow copies the native file into the model dir (otherwise _load_pyfunc receives a path with no model file). Either way, add a regression test that logs a real/fake .rsglm and asserts mlflow.pyfunc.load_model(uri) succeeds and exposes the signature, so the loader-module contract is enforced going forward. The current "log signature for drift detection only" intent should be made explicit if the flavor is deliberately not meant to be loadable — but advertising a loadable flavor that always errors is the silent-failure being flagged.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. The current branch is wave-2-cache-integrity, which touches _mlflow_io.py heavily (caching/disk-cache/load paths). A fix that adds _load_pyfunc or restructures the pyfunc logging in _mlflow_log.py / _mlflow_io.py could collide with in-flight cache work — coordinate edits to _mlflow_io.py and _find_model_artifact / load_mlflow_model dispatch. The producer side (_mlflow_log.py:471-476) is more isolated and lower-collision.

claim.title: MLflow logging aborts (ValueError) for any model with a Date/Datetime/Decimal/Time/Duration feature dtype
claim.location: src/haute/modelling/_signature.py:14-27,70-73 (_POLARS_TO_MLFLOW + _map_dtype); src/haute/modelling/_training_job.py:124-140 (_polars_dtype_name falls through to str(dtype)); call inside mlflow.start_run at src/haute/modelling/_mlflow_log.py:431-476,200-230
claim.failure_scenario: Feature dtypes for the signature/contract are derived by _polars_dtype_name(schema_df[f].dtype). It collapses integer/float variants to Int64/Float64 and String/Categorical to String, but TEMPORAL/DECIMAL dtypes (pl.Date, pl.Datetime, pl.Time, pl.Decimal, pl.Duration) fall through to str(dtype) (e.g. 'Date', "Datetime(time_unit='us', time_zone=None)"). These strings reach build_signature -> _map_dtype, which only knows {Int64, Float64, String, Boolean} and raises ValueError('Unknown polars dtype ...'). The call happens inside mlflow.start_run() with NO try/except in _build_signature_for_log or _log_model_with_signature, so it propagates and aborts the whole logging run. The native model file and the per-model feature_contract.json were already written by _save_artifacts (which tolerates these dtypes), so the result is a saved-but-unlogged model and a failed MLflow run — a partial, surprising outcome for a legitimate date-feature model.
claim.repro_strategy: Build a small DataFrame with one pl.Date (or pl.Datetime) feature column plus a numeric target. Call build_signature(features=['d'], feature_types={'d':'Date'}, categorical_features=[], target_name='y', target_type='Float64') and observe ValueError. End-to-end: train with MLflow logging enabled on data containing a Date feature and observe _save_artifacts succeeds but log_experiment raises.

verdict.repro_outcome: All 5 assertion groups passed. Key output lines: Part 1 — _polars_dtype_name fall-through names: {'Date':'Date', 'Datetime':"Datetime(time_unit='us', time_zone=None)", 'Time':'Time', 'Duration':"Duration(time_unit='us')", 'Decimal':'Decimal(precision=18, scale=2)'} (all OUTSIDE the supported {Int64,Float64,String,Boolean}); Part 2 — build_signature raised: "Unknown polars dtype 'Date'. Supported dtypes: ['Boolean','Float64','Int64','String']"; Part 4 — _build_signature_for_log PROPAGATED the same ValueError (no try/except guard at the logging boundary); Part 5 — a Datetime target_type aborts identically. The repro is pure in-memory (no disk I/O, no project root, never touches src/tests/rating).
verdict.evidence: Code trace + execution confirm the full chain. (1) src/haute/modelling/_training_job.py:124-140 _polars_dtype_name collapses only Boolean/String/Categorical/integer/float and FALLS THROUGH to str(dtype) for temporal/decimal — repro shows it returns 'Date', "Datetime(time_unit='us', time_zone=None)", 'Time', "Duration(time_unit='us')", 'Decimal(...)'. These are snapshotted into self._contract_feature_dtypes (line 717, 425) and self._contract_target_dtype (723). (2) _derive_features (1415-1463) does NOT filter by dtype — it takes all columns minus target/weight/offset/fold/id/date/group/exclude, so a pl.Date column not explicitly excluded becomes a feature; there is NO upstream temporal/decimal rejection anywhere in src/haute/modelling. (3) src/haute/modelling/_signature.py:14-27 _POLARS_TO_MLFLOW whitelists only {Int64,Float64,String,Boolean}; _map_dtype raises ValueError('Unknown polars dtype ...') otherwise; build_signature calls _map_dtype for every feature (71) and the target (75). (4) src/haute/modelling/_mlflow_log.py:531-538 _build_signature_for_log calls build_signature with NO try/except (its only try/except, 506-517, wraps .cbm feature-name inspection). (5) _log_model_with_signature (431) calls it inside the `with mlflow.start_run()` block (200/219) with no surrounding handler — contrast line 362-373 where model-card generation IS wrapped in try/except 'never fails the run', proving the signature path is deliberately unguarded. (6) Ordering: run() calls _save_artifacts at 504-510 (writes native model file + per-model feature_contract.json) BEFORE _log_to_mlflow at 542-545. build_contract (_feature_contract.py:96-134) stores feature_types verbatim (line 127) without _map_dtype validation, so the contract tolerates 'Date'/'Datetime(...)'. Net result: model file + contract land on disk, then log_experiment aborts with ValueError — a saved-but-unlogged model and failed MLflow run, exactly as claimed.
verdict.blast_radius: Any training run with MLflow logging enabled (self.mlflow_experiment set) whose derived feature set — or target — has a pl.Date/Datetime/Time/Decimal/Duration dtype. With feature_columns unset, _derive_features keeps every non-excluded column, so a raw date/decimal column passed through to training triggers it. The native model file and per-model feature_contract.json are written first, so the failure mode is a partial, surprising outcome (model on disk, MLflow run aborted), not a clean fail-fast. Does not affect the deploy-side _build_signature (haute.deploy._mlflow), which intentionally coerces unknown dtypes to string. Scope limited to the modelling MLflow logging path; non-MLflow training (mlflow_experiment unset) is unaffected. Whether real CatBoost/GLM training reaches this point depends on the algo accepting a raw temporal/decimal feature, but no haute-level guard prevents the dtype from arriving here.
verdict.recommended_fix: Extend the dtype-name canonicalisation so temporal/decimal map to an MLflow-representable type rather than falling through to str(dtype). Minimal: in _signature.py add Date->DataType.datetime (or .long), Datetime/Time->DataType.datetime, Duration->DataType.long, Decimal->DataType.double to _POLARS_TO_MLFLOW, and teach _polars_dtype_name (_training_job.py) to emit those canonical names (e.g. map pl.Date/Datetime/Time->'Datetime', pl.Duration->'Int64', pl.Decimal->'Float64') so feature_types and the contract agree with the signature. Whatever mapping is chosen, keep _build_signature_for_log fail-loud for genuinely-unknown dtypes but ensure the common temporal/decimal cases are covered. Add a TDD failing test mirroring the repro (build_signature with 'Date' feature and a Datetime target) plus an integration assertion that a Date-feature training run with MLflow logging completes without aborting after _save_artifacts.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Low. Current branch is wave-2-cache-integrity (cache/integrity work); the modelling signature/MLflow-logging code is not in that hot path. _signature.py and _mlflow_log.py are small, focused modules with dedicated test files (tests/test_mlflow_signature.py) so a fix is unlikely to collide with in-flight cache work.

claim.title: Feature-contract drift check cannot detect Float32-vs-Float64 / Int32-vs-Int64 schema drift (dtype-family collapse)
claim.location: src/haute/deploy/_scorer.py:407-420 (_canonical_dtype) vs src/haute/modelling/_training_job.py:124-140 (_polars_dtype_name); compared in assert_contracts_match src/haute/modelling/_feature_contract.py:485-502
claim.failure_scenario: Both training-time contract construction and deploy-time runtime-contract reconstruction map ALL integer widths to 'Int64' and ALL float widths to 'Float64' (and String/Categorical both to 'String'). assert_contracts_match compares these canonical strings. Therefore if a model was trained on a Float64 feature but at deploy/score time the same feature arrives as Float32 (e.g. an upstream cast, a different parquet writer, a CatBoost-style downcast leaking upstream), the drift check passes even though the numeric representation differs. CatBoost itself casts to Float32 internally so predictions may be unaffected, but the contract's advertised guarantee ('dtype change fails loudly') does not hold at sub-family granularity, and a genuinely meaningful String<->Categorical or numeric-width change is invisible to the actuarial drift gate.
claim.repro_strategy: Build a contract with feature_types={'x':'Float64'} via build_contract, then build an 'actual' contract from a live schema where x is Float32 — note _canonical_dtype(pl.Float32) == 'Float64', so assert_contracts_match does NOT raise. Compare against the architecture invariant that dtype changes should be detected.

verdict.evidence: Ran an isolated in-memory repro exercising the real functions. Output: `[A] _canonical_dtype(Float32)='Float64'  _canonical_dtype(Float64)='Float64'`; `[A] _canonical_dtype(Categorical)='String'  _canonical_dtype(Utf8)='String'`; `[B] _polars_dtype_name(Float32)='Float64'  _polars_dtype_name(Int32)='Int64'`; `[C] trained feature_types={'x':'Float64'} runtime feature_types={'x':'Float64'} drift_gate_passes(no error)=True` (and contract_hash collided); `[D] Int64-vs-Int32 drift_gate_passes=True`; `[E] String-vs-Categorical drift_gate_passes=True`; `[CONTROL] Float64-vs-Int64 drift_gate_passes=False` (gate is alive, so the blindness is specifically sub-family/String-Categorical, not inertness). Code trace confirms the data flow: training builds feature_types via `_training_job.py:717 {f:_polars_dtype_name(...)}`, deploy rebuilds it via `_scorer.py:361-362 _canonical_dtype(...)`, and `assert_contracts_match` (`_feature_contract.py:493-496`) iterates `_FIELDS` (which includes `feature_types`) comparing those collapsed strings. No backstop exists: the loud-validation MLflow signature (`_signature.py:14-19`) only knows the four collapsed families and is fed from the already-collapsed contract; the width-aware map in `_mlflow.py:221-237` operates on `resolved.input_schema` (the deploy pipeline-input schema), not the model feature contract, so it does not guard this path.
verdict.repro_outcome: Exited 0 (REPRODUCED). assert_contracts_match did NOT raise for Float64-vs-Float32, Int64-vs-Int32, or String-vs-Categorical; contract_hash collided for Float64-vs-Float32; the cross-family Float64-vs-Int64 control was correctly detected (raised). Each assertion checks the specific wrong value/behaviour, not merely "something raised". No real project files, rating/, src/, or tests/ were read or written — disk root pinned to a tempfile dir via haute._sandbox.set_project_root.
verdict.blast_radius: The feature-contract drift gate's advertised guarantee ("dtype change fails loudly") holds only at dtype-family granularity. A feature trained as Float64 but arriving at score time as Float32 (upstream cast, different parquet writer, downcast leaking upstream), or Int64-vs-Int32, or String-vs-Categorical, passes the gate silently and even yields an identical contract_hash. Practical impact is bounded: CatBoost casts inputs to Float32 internally, so the Float32/Float64 numeric distinction usually does not change predictions; the String<->Categorical case is more semantically meaningful but uncommon to hit. This is a contract-precision/correctness gap and a weaker-than-advertised actuarial drift assertion, not active data corruption. There is no independent backstop on the in-process scoring path that would catch sub-family drift.
verdict.recommended_fix: Decide on the intended granularity and make it consistent end-to-end. If sub-family width is meant to be pinned: stop collapsing in both canonicalisers (`_canonical_dtype` and `_polars_dtype_name`) — emit the actual width strings (Float32/Float64, Int32/Int64) and split String vs Categorical — and extend the loud MLflow `_signature._POLARS_TO_MLFLOW` map (and `build_signature`) to accept those widths so contract-build stays loud. If family-granularity is intentional (defensible given CatBoost's internal Float32 cast), then update the docstrings/guarantee wording in `_feature_contract.py` and the two canonicaliser docstrings to state explicitly that drift detection is family-level, so operators do not over-trust it. Either way, add a regression test asserting Float64-vs-Float32 and String-vs-Categorical produce the chosen behaviour (raise, or documented-pass).
verdict.coordinate_risk: Low-to-moderate. The three implicated files were last modified in wave 4a/4b (training-lifecycle/deploy-artifacts) work, not the current `wave-2-cache-integrity` branch, so no direct overlap is evident. However `_scorer.py` and `_training_job.py` are broad, frequently-touched files; an in-flight deploy/actuarial-modelling wave could collide. The fix surface is small and localized (three dtype-mapping functions plus one signature map), keeping merge risk contained.

claim.title: Hash-bucket group split and temporal holdout give no guarantee on realised validation/holdout fraction
claim.location: src/haute/modelling/_split.py:191-212 (_assign_group_split), 323-366 (_group_mask), 265-321 (_temporal_mask)
claim.failure_scenario: _group_mask/_assign_group_split assign each unique group to validation/holdout iff md5(seed:group)[:8]/2^32 < threshold — a Bernoulli draw per group. With few groups or skewed group sizes, the realised row-fraction in validation/holdout can be far from the requested validation_size (e.g. request 0.2, get one giant group = 0.6 of rows, or 0 groups triggering only the 'force one group' fallback). The fallback only fires when ZERO groups land in validation; it never corrects an over- or under-shoot. Reported validation/holdout metrics and any early-stopping / model selection driven off them are then computed on a mis-sized, statistically biased split with no error. Temporal holdout sorts post-cutoff rows by arg_sort of dates with possible ties, so tie-break ordering (Polars-version-dependent) decides which equal-date rows fall in holdout vs validation.
claim.repro_strategy: DataFrame with a 'grp' column of e.g. 5 groups of very unequal sizes; SplitConfig(strategy='group', validation_size=0.2, group_column='grp'); call split_mask and measure (partition==1).sum()/n_rows — show it deviates substantially from 0.2 across several seeds. For temporal: rows with many identical dates straddling the validation/holdout boundary; show holdout membership depends on arg_sort tie handling.

verdict.evidence: Ran review/02-findings/repro/modelling__group-temporal-split-fraction-drift.py (uv run, polars 1.39.2). PART 1 (group split, 5 unequal groups A=600,B=250,C=100,D=40,E=10, requested validation_size=0.2): "seeds with |realised - requested| > 0.10 : 21/30"; "WORST seed=2: realised validation fraction = 0.950 (deviation 0.750)"; seed=2 routes the 600-row group 'A' into validation. PART 1b: "seed=19: only tiny group 'E' (10 rows) in validation -> realised fraction = 0.010 (requested 0.2)" — a NON-EMPTY validation group still leaves the fraction at 0.01, and the fallback never corrects it (it fires only when ZERO groups land in validation, _split.py:209-211 / 351-358). PART 2 (temporal, 10 rows all dated 2024-09-01, holdout=5): identity input order -> holdout markers {5,6,7,8,9}; reversed input order -> {0,1,2,3,4}; holdout count =5 both times. Separately confirmed pl.Series.arg_sort is stable by default (returns [0..9] on all-equal keys), so tie membership is decided purely by input row order. Control: 200 equal-sized groups land near target (mean 0.200, range 0.13-0.23), proving the drift is specific to few/skewed groups, not a blanket mis-assignment. Code trace: _group_mask (_split.py:323-366) is a per-group Bernoulli draw md5(seed:group)[:8]/2^32 < threshold; the only correction (lines 352-358) triggers solely on no_validation. _temporal_mask (_split.py:300-314) sorts non-train rows by arg_sort of dates (ties resolved by input order) and slices the last n_holdout as holdout. Downstream _training_job.py:777-784 (_compute_split) and _evaluate just count n_validation/n_holdout from the produced mask and compute metrics on those partitions — no check that realised fraction matches requested size, and no docstring in _split.py warns the fraction is approximate.
verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (all assertions). Demonstrated realised group-split validation fraction of 0.950 and 0.010 vs requested 0.200, with no correction for a non-empty validation group; and tie-dependent temporal holdout membership ({5,6,7,8,9} vs {0,1,2,3,4}) among 10 identical-date rows.
verdict.blast_radius: Affects any training run using strategy="group" with few or size-skewed groups, and strategy="temporal" with holdout_size>0 where many rows share the cutoff-adjacent date. Validation/holdout row counts can deviate massively (seen 0.01x-4.75x the requested size). Reported validation/holdout metrics, diagnostics-set selection (holdout>validation>train in _evaluate), and any early-stopping/model selection driven off the validation partition are then computed on a mis-sized, higher-variance split with no error or warning. Determinism for a fixed seed AND fixed input row order is preserved (groups stay intact, arg_sort stable today), so it is not a crash or data-corruption bug — it is a silent statistical-quality/expectation gap. Temporal tie membership additionally depends on upstream row ordering and on arg_sort's stability remaining unchanged across Polars versions.
verdict.recommended_fix: Two small, independent mitigations. (1) Group split: after building group_partition, compute realised validation/holdout row fractions and, when they deviate beyond a tolerance (or when n_unique_groups is small), emit a loud logger.warning naming requested vs realised fractions and the group count — surfacing the foot-gun rather than silently proceeding; optionally document in the _group_mask/_assign_group_split docstrings that the fraction is approximate and degrades with few/skewed groups. (2) Temporal holdout: make the tie ordering explicit and deterministic — break ties on a stable secondary key (e.g. row index) via arg_sort with a defined order, or document that equal-date rows at the boundary are partitioned by input order, so behaviour does not silently change with Polars sort internals. Per repo CLAUDE.md, prefer fail-loud/warn-loud over a silent approximation; do not add a fallback that masks the issue.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. src/haute/modelling/_split.py and _training_job.py sit in the Modelling: training/scoring/MLflow subsystem; the current branch is wave-2-cache-integrity (cache work, not modelling), but recent commits touch rating-optimiser/projection regression CI, and split logic is adjacent to training pipelines that other in-flight modelling work may edit. Any fix is localized to _split.py (plus an optional warning hook in _compute_split) and is unlikely to conflict, but coordinate if a modelling-split or evaluation feature branch is concurrently active.

claim.title: Cancelled GPU CatBoost fit can leak a live worker thread, the held Pool/model, and the train_dir
claim.location: src/haute/modelling/_algorithms.py:335-445 (_run_gpu_fit_with_metric_polling), 547-557 (fit dispatch)
claim.failure_scenario: GPU training runs model.fit on a daemon worker thread while the main thread polls learn_error.tsv. On cancellation, on_iteration raises; the helper joins the worker for at most _GPU_FIT_ABORT_JOIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (30s). CatBoost cannot be interrupted mid-fit, so if the fit is still running after 30s the helper logs gpu_fit_thread_zombie_after_cancel, annotates the exception, and re-raises WITHOUT removing train_dir and while the worker (holding the CatBoost model + Pool + GPU/host memory) keeps running and writing files. Repeated cancellations of long GPU fits accumulate zombie threads and orphaned train_dir directories; only the route-layer single-job lock prevents a new job from starting, but the abandoned writer is still live. Loudly logged but unrecoverable in-process.
claim.repro_strategy: Hard to reproduce without a GPU. Substitute a fake fit() that sleeps > abort timeout and an on_iteration that raises BackgroundJobStoppedError on first call; assert _run_gpu_fit_with_metric_polling re-raises, leaves train_dir present, and the worker thread is still alive (worker.is_alive() True) after the call.

verdict.evidence: Ran a minimal repro (Event-gated fit that outlives a 0.05s abort_join_timeout, on_iteration raising a cancellation). All three claimed facts confirmed: (a) helper re-raised the cancellation (_CancelledForTestError); (c) worker.is_alive() == True immediately after the helper returned, with fit_not_finished == True (genuine zombie, not already-completed); (b) train_dir still present after the call. The error log fired: `gpu_fit_thread_zombie_after_cancel ... thread_name=catboost-gpu-fit train_dir=...`, and the exception note read "CatBoost GPU fit thread 'catboost-gpu-fit' was still running 0.05s after cancellation; train_dir ... was left in place for the live writer." Code trace matches: at _algorithms.py:409 `on_iteration(...)` is called OUTSIDE the parse-guard try, so the cancellation propagates to `except BaseException` at line 419; line 424 joins with abort_join_timeout_seconds; line 425 finds the worker (daemon thread, line 379, holding the closure over model+pool) still alive; lines 426-437 log + add_note + `raise`, bypassing the `shutil.rmtree(train_dir, ...)` at line 438. The worker keeps the CatBoost model + Pool + GPU/host memory live. HOWEVER: this is intentional, documented, and already tested behaviour, not an undiscovered defect. The function docstring (lines 350-362) defines this as the "Lifecycle contract (remediation 4b.7 ... no leaked train_dir)" and explicitly justifies retaining train_dir ("removing files under a live CatBoost writer would half-destroy its working dir") and the loud abandon. tests/test_gpu_fit_cancel.py::test_zombie_worker_is_loud_and_train_dir_retained (lines 154-205) already asserts exactly this (re-raise + note + error log + train_dir.exists() True). The claim itself concedes severity low / "Loudly logged but unrecoverable in-process".

claim.title: GLM coefficient/relativity fallbacks guard only on array length, not name/coef ordering or intercept identity

claim.title: PolarsFanInRule passthrough-parent inference routes ALL uncovered columns to a single heuristically-chosen parent, which can demand a column from a parent that does not produce it
claim.location: src/haute/projection.py:1480-1515 (missing-column passthrough), :1839-1852 (simple_left_join_passthrough_parent), :1824-1836 (unambiguous_passthrough_parent)
claim.failure_scenario: For a multi-parent POLARS fan-in whose declared inputs_by_parent does not cover all base_contribution columns, the rule attributes the remaining 'missing' columns to one passthrough parent: either the sole left parent of inferred simple left/semi/anti joins (simple_left_join_passthrough_parent), or the single parent whose declaration is a subset of `referenced` (unambiguous_passthrough_parent). Both are heuristics over an AST parse that can be incomplete (aliasing it cannot resolve, a left-join chain where the genuine producer of the missing column is actually the RIGHT parent, or `referenced` failing to disambiguate). If the wrong parent is chosen, the edge projection demands the column from a parent that does not produce it. Under a strict profile (DEPLOY_BATCH / lazy sink) the lazy engine narrows that parent's scan to include a column it cannot supply -> at best a loud ProjectionImpossible/missing-column failure (acceptable), but if the mis-chosen parent COINCIDENTALLY has a same-named column, projection reads the wrong physical column into the join -> a semantically wrong narrowed batch/deploy read with no error. This is the densest multi-parent silent-correctness surface and the invariant 'never silently route a column to the wrong parent' depends entirely on these heuristics being conservative.
claim.repro_strategy: Construct a 2-parent POLARS node with code doing `left.join(right, on='k', how='left')` plus a `with_columns` that references a column present in BOTH parents under the same name but produced/owned by the right parent, with inputs_by_parent under-declared so that column is 'missing'. Run compute_prepared_plan(strict_projection=True) and inspect edge_demands: assert the column is demanded from `left` (the inferred passthrough) rather than the true producer. Needs a careful adversarial graph; classified testable but intricate.

verdict.evidence: Executed repro (review/02-findings/repro/projection-trace__fan-in-passthrough-parent-misroute.py). Key output: ground-truth Polars check across all join types shows the UN-SUFFIXED collision column `c` is ALWAYS owned by the LEFT operand (inner/left/outer/full/right/semi: c=['L1','L2']; the right copy becomes `c_right`). Scenario A (the claim's exact recipe, how='left'): shared_col routed to left = ['k','shared_col'] -> CORRECT, refuting the literal claim. Scenario C (inner join, asymmetric over-declared contract inputs_by_parent={left:['k','left_only'], right:['k']} with left_only NOT in node inputs): shared_col routed to RIGHT only (left demand=['k']); replaying projected scans through Polars silently changes out_col from [112,223] (correct, left-owned) to [778,889] (wrong, right value) with NO error. Trace: simple_left_join_passthrough_parent (projection.py:1839) returns None for how='inner' (not in {left,semi,anti}); unambiguous_passthrough_parent (projection.py:1824) then picks RIGHT as the sole `cols<=referenced` candidate because LEFT is disqualified by left_only. _apply_edge_projection (_execute_lazy.py:1028-1059) narrows LEFT's scan to {k} WITHOUT error -- its missing-column guard at line 1046 only catches OVER-demanding, never UNDER-demanding the correct parent. Controls confirm: self-consistent and symmetric-over-declared contracts both raise ContractMismatchError loudly (safe). Contract.from_user_declared (_contracts.py:63-108) performs NO cross-validation of inputs_by_parent against inputs/parent schemas, so the triggering contract is accepted.
verdict.repro_outcome: REPRODUCED a silent misroute, but NOT via the claim's stated recipe. The claim's literal left-join scenario routes CORRECTLY (un-suffixed collision column is owned by the LEFT operand in every Polars join type, so routing to left is right; how='left' also never reaches the questioned heuristic). The real bug surfaces for a non-{left,semi,anti} join (inner/outer/full/right/cross) where simple_left_join_passthrough_parent returns None and unambiguous_passthrough_parent picks RIGHT because the semantically-correct LEFT parent is disqualified by an over-declared column (a parent column not in the node's `inputs`). Then shared_col (owned by LEFT) is demanded only from RIGHT, _apply_edge_projection silently drops it from LEFT's scan with no error, and the join substitutes the RIGHT value (out_col [112,223] -> [778,889]). Reachable but narrow: requires asymmetric over-declared inputs_by_parent; self-consistent and symmetric contracts fail loudly.
verdict.blast_radius: Multi-parent POLARS fan-in nodes that (a) use an inner/outer/full/right/cross join between the two incoming parents, (b) reference a non-key column present in BOTH parents under the same un-suffixed name, and (c) have an `inputs_by_parent` contract where exactly the semantically-correct (left-operand) parent over-declares a column not in the node's `inputs`, disqualifying it as the subset candidate so the heuristic resolves to the wrong (right) parent. Result is a silent wrong physical read: the join output's un-suffixed column carries the right parent's values instead of the left's, with no error. The common left/semi/anti-join path is unaffected (routes correctly via simple_left_join_passthrough_parent), and self-consistent / symmetric contracts fail loudly rather than silently. The strict (DEPLOY_BATCH/lazy-sink) profile does not add a guard -- routing is profile-independent and _apply_edge_projection's guard only catches over-demand. Narrow trigger surface but a genuine silent-correctness hole on deploy/batch reads.
verdict.recommended_fix: Make unambiguous_passthrough_parent conservative when a join is present: when simple_left_join_passthrough_parent returns None but joins WERE inferred (a real left operand exists), do NOT fall back to the subset heuristic for un-suffixed collision columns -- instead route the un-suffixed missing column to the LEFT operand of the relevant join (the true Polars owner), or fail loudly with ContractMismatchError rather than guess. More fundamentally, add cross-validation in declared_inputs_by_parent / Contract.from_user_declared that each parent's inputs_by_parent columns are a subset of the node's declared `inputs` (and ideally of that parent's produced schema), so an over-declared column can never silently disqualify the correct parent. A failing test should pin: an inner-join 2-parent node with a shared non-key column and an asymmetric over-declared contract must EITHER route shared_col to the left operand OR raise -- never demand it only from the right parent.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Yes -- this sits squarely in src/haute/projection.py (the Projection & price tracing subsystem) on the wave-2-cache-integrity branch, in the exact passthrough-inference functions an in-flight projection/cache-integrity feature branch is most likely to be touching. (2) modelling.py:82-90: the status-endpoint non-finite branch calls _store.atomic_update(job_id, {"status":"error","message":...,"result":None}, expected_status="completed") -- terminal_reason is NOT among the fields. (3) _job_store.py:252 (_store_merged_job_locked): merged = {**old, **fields}, so old terminal_reason="completed" survives the merge; nothing clears it. (4) modelling.py:121 builds TrainStatusResponse(terminal_reason=job.get("terminal_reason")) and schemas.py:874 declares terminal_reason: str|None with no enum constraint, so 'completed' passes through unchanged. Repro stdout: "observed status = 'error'", "observed terminal_reason = 'completed'", "REPRODUCED: ... status='error' but terminal_reason='completed'." Existing test tests/test_modelling_routes.py:665 (test_non_finite_completed_result_becomes_job_error) exercises this very branch but creates the job via create_job({"status":"completed",...}) WITHOUT terminal_reason and never asserts on it -> the inconsistency is a genuine uncovered gap. Reachability caveat (honest): the worker validates the SAME immutable TrainResponse object at _train_service.py:1147 immediately before storing it at line 1153, and the endpoint re-validates that same object via the identical _assert_json_finite; there is no path that mutates a stored completed result. So for a normally-completed job whose result genuinely passed the worker guard, the endpoint guard also passes and this error branch does NOT fire. The inconsistent (error, completed) record is produced only when a non-finite value reaches a completed job's stored result -- precisely the situation this defensive guard exists to catch (e.g. a future store-without-transition path, or a container type the recursive walk does not yet descend). When the guard does fire, it emits a self-contradicting terminal state. This matches the claim's stated scenario and its 'low' severity.
verdict.blast_radius: A single job's status record: the response reports status='error' (correct, dominant signal) but terminal_reason='completed' (stale/wrong). Frontend consumers read terminal_reason (frontend/src/hooks/useBackgroundJobs.ts, ExecutionDiagnosticsSummary, ModellingConfig/OptimiserConfig status mapping), so a diagnostics panel could mislabel an errored job as completed; however the primary status='error' remains correct so the most prominent UI state is right. Only the 'training' namespace status endpoint is affected; the optimiser/explore equivalents are not implicated by this specific call site. Triggers only on the defensive non-finite-result branch, which does not fire for normally-validated completed results.
verdict.recommended_fix: Route the error flip through the lifecycle so status and terminal_reason stay coherent: replace the raw _store.atomic_update at modelling.py:82-90 with self._lifecycle.transition(job_id, to="error", message=message, fields={"result": None}, expected_status="completed") (or, minimally, add "terminal_reason": "error" to the atomic_update fields dict). Then extend tests/test_modelling_routes.py::test_non_finite_completed_result_becomes_job_error to first create the job via JobLifecycle.transition(to="completed") (so terminal_reason="completed" is present) and assert data["terminal_reason"] == "error" after the poll -- locking in the invariant that status and terminal_reason agree.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. The current branch is wave-2-cache-integrity and touches the job store / cache-integrity area; modelling.py:71-107 and _job_store.atomic_update are exactly the kind of code an in-flight cache/lifecycle branch may be editing (the _result_finite_validated caching block sits adjacent). A fixer should rebase/coordinate so the lifecycle-routed error transition does not collide with concurrent changes to the validation-cache block or to atomic_update's merge semantics.

claim.title: JobStore.jobs returns the underlying _jobs dict by reference (no copy, no lock); callers iterate/subscript it outside _write_lock, and JobLifecycle.transition reaches into store.jobs[job_id] + store._write_lock directly — the 'all mutation linearises on _write_lock' invariant rests on external caller discipline, not encapsulation
claim.location: src/haute/routes/_job_store.py:533-541 (jobs property); src/haute/routes/_job_lifecycle.py:136-167 (reaches into store.jobs[job_id], store._write_lock, store._store_merged_job_locked); raw readers in _optimiser_service.py (see optimiser-worker-raw-jobs-keyerror)
claim.failure_scenario: Any code holding the dict returned by `.jobs` can observe a torn view or trigger 'dict changed size during iteration' if a writer's whole-dict swap or _evict_stale() pop runs concurrently. On free-threaded CPython 3.13 (which routes/_helpers.py:319-324 explicitly anticipates for ws_clients) the single-reference reads the property relies on are no longer GIL-atomic, so the lock-free reads become genuinely unsynchronised. JobLifecycle.transition re-implements the locked read-merge-swap by poking three private JobStore members (store.jobs[job_id], store._write_lock, store._store_merged_job_locked); the encapsulation that is supposed to guarantee linearisation is therefore distributed across two modules and every ad-hoc `.jobs` reader, making the invariant fragile to the next caller that forgets the discipline.
claim.repro_strategy: Code-trace argument plus a stress harness: spawn one thread doing repeated store.atomic_update/create_job/get_job (which evicts) and another iterating `for k in store.jobs: store.jobs[k]`; on CPython you may catch a RuntimeError('dictionary changed size during iteration'). The design point (reference leak + private-member reach-in) is provable by reading the two cited locations; the race is best demonstrated rather than asserted deterministically.

verdict.repro_outcome: Ran on CPython 3.11.13 (GIL=True). (1) DESIGN FACT TRUE: `.jobs is store._jobs` and external mutation of the returned dict is visible via the store -> reference leak confirmed. (2) F1: id(store._jobs) is unchanged across 200 writes -> the claim's 'whole-dict swap' does not exist in code. (3) F2: a reader grabbing `store.jobs[jc]` and reading two correlated fields off that reference saw 0 torn observations across 200,000 reads while a writer continuously flipped both fields -> 'torn view' is impossible. (4) F3: with a churner adding+popping keys 400,000 times (constant dict size change), single-key subscript `store.jobs[f"k{i%64}"]` raised 'dictionary changed size during iteration' ZERO times; it raised KeyError 43,750 times -- and KeyError is the SEPARATE cross-referenced sibling finding optimiser-worker-raw-jobs-keyerror, not this one. All assertions passed; the runtime failure_scenario did not reproduce.
verdict.evidence: Code facts (true part): _job_store.py:533-541 `jobs` property returns `self._jobs` with no copy/lock; _job_lifecycle.py:136-167 holds `with self.store._write_lock` then reaches into `store.jobs[job_id]` and `store._store_merged_job_locked` (3 private members across a module boundary). These design observations are accurate. BUT the falsifiable runtime claims are wrong: (a) `self._jobs` is NEVER rebound after __init__ (Grep `self\._jobs\s*=` -> no matches), so there is no 'whole-dict swap' to observe. (b) Every writer (_store_merged_job_locked:255, _clear_heavy_objects_locked:199, clear_result_data:531) does `self._jobs[job_id] = <fresh dict>` -- it swaps a brand-new dict at the key, never mutates in place; the docstring at atomic_update lines 389-401 states this is serialised on _write_lock and that `dict.__setitem__` atomicity means 'a reader will always see either the old dict or the new one - never a half-updated state'. So a reader holding `old = store.jobs[job_id]` has a frozen, consistent snapshot -> no torn view. (c) The 'dict changed size during iteration' RuntimeError requires concurrent ITERATION, but NO real caller iterates `.jobs`: Grep `for .* in .*\.jobs|\.jobs\.values\(\)|\.jobs\.items\(\)` over src/ -> 0 hits; every callsite (_optimiser_service.py:2188 uses `.get(job_id,{})`, :3478+ use `[job_id]`, _job_lifecycle.py:137 is INSIDE the lock) does a single-key subscript, which can only KeyError, never raise that RuntimeError. (d) Free-threaded framing is moot: pyproject `requires-python=">=3.11"`, interpreter is 3.11.13 with GIL enabled; the _helpers.py:319-324 comment is forward-looking prose about ws_clients, not a statement that the deployment runs --disable-gil. Net: design-smell is real but its predicted failure (whole-dict swap / torn view / size-change RuntimeError) is refuted; the only real defect from the leak (bare-subscript KeyError) is already owned by the cross-referenced sibling finding optimiser-worker-raw-jobs-keyerror.

claim.title: load_sidecar swallows corrupt .haute.json (JSONDecodeError/OSError/ValueError) to {} with only a warning, silently dropping all node positions, declared sources, and active_source — a quiet UX/state regression that contradicts the project fail-loud mandate, asymmetric with pipeline_dir which raises ConfigError on a malformed haute.toml
claim.location: src/haute/routes/_helpers.py:622-634 (load_sidecar) vs 110-173 (pipeline_dir raises ConfigError); consumed by parse_pipeline_to_graph at 725-751
claim.failure_scenario: A .haute.json sidecar gets partially written or corrupted by external tooling / an interrupted write. On the next GET /api/pipeline (or any parse_pipeline_to_graph), load_sidecar catches the decode error, logs warning('corrupt_sidecar'), and returns {}. parse_pipeline_to_graph then applies no positions (every node snaps to default), resets sources to ['live'] and active_source to 'live'. The user silently loses their canvas layout and their selected data source — and because the next save rewrites the sidecar from the now-default in-memory graph, the corruption is converted into permanent data loss with no loud error at any point. Note save_sidecar itself uses atomic_write_text precisely to avoid producing such torn files, but the read side still degrades silently if a torn/corrupt file exists from any other cause.
claim.repro_strategy: Write a pipeline .py plus a sibling .haute.json containing invalid JSON (e.g. '{ broken'). Call parse_pipeline_to_graph(py_path) and assert it returns successfully with empty positions and sources==['live'] (i.e. it did NOT raise), demonstrating the silent drop. Contrast with pipeline_dir() against a malformed haute.toml which raises ConfigError. Tiny standalone fs fixture; no server needed.

verdict.evidence: Executed repro reproduced every behavioral assertion. Key output lines: (1) `[warning] corrupt_sidecar ... file=pipeline.haute.json` then `[caseB] load_sidecar returned {} (no exception)` — confirms src/haute/routes/_helpers.py:632-634 swallows JSONDecodeError to {} with only a warning. (2) `[caseB corrupt sidecar] target pos={'x':0.0,'y':0.0} sources=['live'] active=live` while the control case A (valid sidecar) gave `pos={'x':4242.0,'y':9999.0} sources=['live','snapshot_2024'] active=snapshot_2024` — proving parse_pipeline_to_graph (725-751) silently drops the custom position, declared sources, and active_source when the sidecar is corrupt, reverting to parser defaults. (3) `[caseC] pipeline_dir() RAISED ConfigError: haute.toml is malformed` — confirms the asymmetry with _helpers.py:142-148. The behavior is exactly as claimed. IMPORTANT CONTEXT: this fail-soft is INTENTIONAL and pinned by tests — tests/test_partial_failure.py:594 TestCorruptSidecar ("Corrupt .haute.json must not prevent pipeline loading"), tests/test_route_helpers.py:245 test_corrupt_json, tests/test_server.py:3544 test_corrupt_json_returns_empty all assert load_sidecar(corrupt)=={}. The sidecar is explicitly documented (SidecarModel docstring, _helpers.py:34-58) as editor-state metadata, NOT the source of truth (the .py is). So the factual claim is real but it is a deliberate availability-over-fail-loud tradeoff for non-authoritative state, not an accidental defect.
verdict.repro_outcome: REPRODUCED (exit 0). load_sidecar(corrupt) -> {} with no exception; parse_pipeline_to_graph silently reverted custom position {4242,9999}->{0,0}, sources->['live'], active_source->'live'; pipeline_dir(malformed toml) raised ConfigError (asymmetry confirmed). Control case A (valid sidecar honoured) passed, so the case-B loss is attributable to corruption, not a broken merge path.
verdict.blast_radius: Any GET /api/pipeline or file-watcher reparse over a pipeline whose sibling .haute.json is corrupt/torn from external cause. User-visible effect: canvas layout snaps all nodes to default (0,0) and the selected non-'live' data source resets to 'live'. The .py pipeline source of truth is unaffected — graph topology, node code, and edges all load correctly. The claimed escalation to 'permanent data loss' requires the user to then SAVE on top of the reset state (not demonstrated, and is a separate user action); it is recoverable until then. save_sidecar itself uses atomic_write_text so haute never PRODUCES torn files; this only bites if an external/interrupted writer creates one.
verdict.recommended_fix: Contested whether a fix is warranted — the current fail-soft is deliberate and test-pinned (changing it to raise would re-break the 3 TestCorruptSidecar/test_corrupt_json tests that guarantee a corrupt sidecar never makes the pipeline inaccessible). If the team wants to honour the fail-loud mandate without losing availability, the minimal non-destructive improvement is: on corrupt sidecar, (a) keep returning {} for load so the pipeline still opens, but (b) escalate the log from warning to error and surface a non-blocking UI banner ('canvas layout could not be read — saving will overwrite it'), and (c) on the next save, refuse to silently clobber a sidecar that previously failed to parse (e.g. rename the corrupt file to .haute.json.corrupt first) so the torn file is preserved for recovery rather than overwritten. Do NOT make load_sidecar raise — that regresses the pinned availability invariant. Note: ValueError/TypeError in the except clause are broad and could also mask genuine programming bugs in dict(_json.loads(...)); narrowing to JSONDecodeError|OSError|UnicodeDecodeError would tighten it.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. src/haute/routes/_helpers.py load_sidecar/save_sidecar/parse_pipeline_to_graph sit in the sidecar/atomic-write hot path that the current branch (wave-2-cache-integrity, with recent Bundle 5.M2 atomic-write work and 'cache integrity' theme) is actively touching. Any change here must keep TestSaveSidecar.test_writes_atomically_via_atomic_write_text and the TestCorruptSidecar suite green. Low risk of merge conflict with model/projection work, but high overlap with in-flight cache/sidecar integrity changes.

claim.title: _RequestIdMiddleware trusts a client-supplied x-request-id verbatim (no length/charset bound) and reflects it into every structlog line and back into the response x-request-id header — log-injection / response-header-injection via an unbounded reflected value
claim.location: src/haute/server.py:370 (rid = request.headers.get('x-request-id', ...)), 372 (bind_contextvars), 396 (response.headers['x-request-id'] = rid)
claim.failure_scenario: A request arrives with x-request-id set to an attacker-controlled value containing newlines/CR/LF or a very large string. The middleware binds it unmodified into the structlog contextvars so it is emitted on every log line for the request (enabling forged/!split log entries in any aggregator that treats newlines as record boundaries), and writes it back into the response header. Although Starlette/h11 will reject raw CR/LF in a header value at send time (mitigating classic HTTP response splitting), the structured-log injection and unbounded-length reflection are not mitigated. Under the single-user local trust model the blast radius is small, but the value is the one piece of fully attacker-controlled, unvalidated data that flows straight into logs and a response header.
claim.repro_strategy: TestClient GET /api/session with header x-request-id='a'*100000 and with x-request-id='line1\nline2'; capture the structlog output and assert the request_id field carries the raw oversized / newline-bearing value (proving no sanitisation). The header-reflection half is shown by asserting response.headers['x-request-id'] echoes the oversized value. Pure middleware test.

verdict.repro_outcome: All assertions PASS through the REAL structlog chain. A2: emitted JSON log request_id == raw 100,000-char value (no length bound). A3: bound contextvar inside request == raw oversized value. A4: response x-request-id header echoes the raw 100,000-char value. B1: emitted log request_id contains the raw newline ('line1\nline2 forged=evil') — no charset sanitisation. B2: newline survives into the bound contextvar. B3 (informational): for the newline value the response x-request-id header was echoed verbatim at status 200 (the Starlette TestClient ASGI transport did not reject a lone LF). NOTE: an initial version using structlog.testing.capture_logs reported A2/B1 as None — that is a harness artifact (capture_logs replaces the whole processor chain with a single LogCapture sink, bypassing merge_contextvars); re-running through configure_logging()'s real chain (first processor = merge_contextvars, src/haute/_logging.py:72) confirmed the verbatim propagation.
verdict.evidence: src/haute/server.py:370 `rid = request.headers.get("x-request-id", uuid.uuid4().hex[:12])` takes the client header verbatim; :372 `structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars(request_id=rid)` binds it unmodified; :396 `response.headers["x-request-id"] = rid` reflects it. Grep over src/ shows x-request-id is referenced ONLY at lines 370/372/396 (plus a docstring in _logging.py) — there is NO length cap or charset validation anywhere, and no upstream middleware mutates it (LocalSessionMiddleware/LocalTrustedHostMiddleware never touch x-request-id). _logging.py:72 places structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars as the first processor, so the bound request_id IS rendered onto every emitted log line. Executed repro confirmed: 100,000-char and raw-newline values both flow verbatim into the rendered JSON log and into the response header. Trust model corroborated: cli/_serve.py defaults the bind host to 127.0.0.1 (loopback) and loudly warns on non-loopback binds, so the realistic attack surface is a malicious web page / curl on localhost, matching the claim's stated low severity.
verdict.blast_radius: The reflected/logged value is the single piece of fully attacker-controlled, unvalidated data on the request path. (1) Structured-log injection: a newline-bearing x-request-id is emitted verbatim in the request_id field on every log line for that request; any log aggregator that treats LF as a record boundary (and console/dev renderer, which does not escape) can be tricked into forged/split log records. In JSON mode the newline is \n-escaped within the JSON string (so it does not break JSON line framing), but the value is still attacker-controlled and unbounded. (2) Unbounded length: a multi-hundred-KB header is bound into contextvars (held for the whole request) and reflected into the response, a minor memory/log-bloat amplification per request. (3) Response-header reflection: classic CRLF HTTP response splitting is mitigated by h11 rejecting CR, but a lone LF and arbitrary-length values can still be reflected (repro showed lone-LF echoed at 200 via TestClient). Confined to a single-user loopback server, so no cross-tenant impact.
verdict.recommended_fix: In _RequestIdMiddleware.dispatch, validate/normalise the inbound header before binding/reflecting: accept it only if it matches a tight pattern (e.g. ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$), otherwise fall back to the generated uuid4().hex[:12]. Bind and reflect the sanitised value. This loudly drops malformed/oversized ids (consistent with the repo's no-silent-fallback ethos by simply regenerating a clean id) and closes both the log-injection and unbounded-reflection vectors. Add a unit test asserting that x-request-id='a'*100000 and x-request-id='line1\nline2' are NOT reflected verbatim into either the log request_id or the response header.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Low-to-moderate. _RequestIdMiddleware sits at the top of the middleware stack in src/haute/server.py — a hot file. The current branch is wave-2-cache-integrity (cache work), so direct overlap is unlikely, but any in-flight branch touching server.py middleware ordering or the logging contract could conflict; the fix is a self-contained ~5-line change confined to the dispatch method, so a rebase is cheap.

claim.title: The status/validity path (post/get json-cache status -> _v2_status_response -> is_per_port_cache_valid) reads an on-disk v2 config WITHOUT running validate_v2_schema, and _v2_fingerprint silently `continue`s past non-dict tables/columns — two distinct malformed configs can collide to the same schema_fingerprint and a stale per-port parquet cache is judged fresh
claim.location: src/haute/routes/json_cache.py:457-475 (_v2_status_response calls is_per_port_cache_valid with unvalidated config), 478-519 (post/get status); src/haute/_json_shred.py:108-147 (_v2_fingerprint skips non-dict entries), 1034-1068 (is_per_port_cache_valid compares schema_fingerprint)
claim.failure_scenario: Unlike /build (which calls validate_v2_schema inside build_per_port_cache, loud-failing B1/B2 violations), the status/validity route only checks freshness. For the on-disk config path (_read_v2_config) no validate_v2_schema runs before is_per_port_cache_valid. _v2_fingerprint defensively skips any table or column that isn't a dict. So a config whose differentiating content lives in a malformed (non-dict) table/column — e.g. a column entry that is a bare string rather than an object — hashes identically to a config without that entry. If a prior build wrote a meta.json whose schema_fingerprint matches this degenerate hash and the data-file signature still matches, is_per_port_cache_valid returns True and the status endpoint reports cached=True against a parquet set that does not reflect the true (malformed-but-meaningful-to-the-user) schema. This is the architecture's documented _v2_fingerprint malformed-table-collision blind spot, reached through the routes' unvalidated validity path.
claim.repro_strategy: Build a per-port cache for a config A, then craft config B identical to A except with an extra column expressed as a non-dict (e.g. a string) — assert _v2_fingerprint(A) == _v2_fingerprint(B), then assert is_per_port_cache_valid(cache_dir_built_for_A, B, data_path=...) returns True (stale judged fresh). Overlaps the wave-2 cache-integrity audit; the routes-specific angle is that the status route never calls validate_v2_schema so B never loud-fails before the freshness compare.

verdict.evidence:
Executed repro (EXIT=0, all asserts pass) at review/02-findings/repro/routes__json-cache-status-validity-skips-schema-validation.py. Key output: "[1] fingerprint(A)=79459e385364bf91 / fingerprint(B)=79459e385364bf91" (collision); "[2] validate_v2_schema(B) raised: v2 tables[0].columns[2] is not a dict" (build would loud-fail B); "[3] is_per_port_cache_valid(cache_for_A, B) = True" (stale-for-B judged fresh); "[4] _v2_status_response(B).cached = True". Config B = config A plus one EXTRA non-dict column (a bare string), built a REAL per-port cache for A in a tempdir.

Code-trace of the missing guard: post_json_cache_status (json_cache.py:478-495) -> _select_v2_config (236-252) / _read_v2_config (179-233) -> _v2_status_response (457-475) -> is_per_port_cache_valid (_json_shred.py:1034-1077). None of these call validate_v2_schema; the build path does (build_per_port_cache, _json_shred.py:776). _v2_fingerprint `continue`s past non-dict tables/columns (_json_shred.py:118-119, 122-123), so A and B hash identically; is_per_port_cache_valid compares only that fingerprint (line 1064) plus a data-file signature (which here matches, since the same data file is used). validate_v2_schema explicitly raises on a non-dict column (_api_input_schema.py:347-350) and non-dict table (306-307).

This also breaks two documented invariants: schemas.py:640-649 states volatile_schema is typed Any *so that* malformed payloads "surface as a 422 from validate_v2_schema" (T8 contract), and json_cache.py:513-515 claims "the precise corruption error surfaces on the build/POST-status paths" — but POST /status never validates, so the non-dict-column corruption class silently yields cached=True instead of a 422.
verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (EXIT=0) — all 4 assertions hold: (1) _v2_fingerprint collision A==B (79459e38...), (2) validate_v2_schema(B) raises ApiInputSchemaError (non-dict column), (3) is_per_port_cache_valid(cache_for_A, B) returns True, (4) _v2_status_response(B).cached is True. Fully isolated: cache written under a tempdir (.../Temp/tmpl1rsq551/.haute_cache/...); no real project / src / tests file touched (stray first-run artifact in .haute_cache cleaned up; git status -- src tests is clean).
verdict.blast_radius: Affects POST and GET /api/json-cache/status only (the validity/freshness path). Two effects: (a) the status endpoint reports cached=True for a v2 config that /build would reject with a structured 422 — a status/build inconsistency and a violation of the project's "fail loudly" rule and the documented T8 / GET-status contracts; (b) two textually-distinct configs that differ only in malformed (non-dict) table/column entries are treated as the same schema, so the "cached" verdict reflects a config the served parquet does not textually match. NOT proven and NOT in scope: corrupted served DATA rows — the data-file signature guard (_data_file_matches) correctly invalidates on edited data files; the only thing mis-judged is schema identity. Real-world reachability is narrow: the malformed entry must be a non-dict column/table, which the normal ApiInputEditor does not emit (volatile_schema comes from React state); it would require a hand-crafted/corrupted apiInput config or a frontend bug emitting a bare string column.

For POST /status, let ApiInputSchemaError propagate to _api_input_schema_error_response (the 422 path already wired at lines 488-489/494-495), honouring the schemas.py:640-649 contract. For GET /status, keep the read-only "corrupt config => cached=False" stance but route it through the same validation (catch ApiInputSchemaError -> cached=False) so the two endpoints agree. This makes the GET docstring claim (lines 513-515) true and closes the _v2_fingerprint non-dict-collision blind spot at the route boundary without changing _v2_fingerprint's defensive iteration (which legitimately must tolerate arbitrary on-disk configs elsewhere).
verdict.coordinate_risk: Medium. This sits squarely in the wave-2 cache-integrity area on branch wave-2-cache-integrity (current branch); _json_shred.py is_per_port_cache_valid / _v2_fingerprint and routes/json_cache.py status handlers are exactly the files an in-flight cache-integrity wave is likely editing. The finder itself flags overlap with the wave-2 cache-integrity audit. Coordinate the fix with that wave to avoid duplicate or conflicting edits; the fix is a small, additive validate_v2_schema call so merge risk is low if sequenced.

claim.title: EventBus GraphUpdatePayload TypedDict declares only {graph, source_file} but the file-watcher publishes {graph, graph_fingerprint, source_file}; the publish/subscribe @overloads advertise the narrow (incomplete) contract while the impl widens to dict[str,Any], so a type-checker cannot catch a subscriber that relies on the declared shape
claim.location: src/haute/_event_bus.py:83-95 (GraphUpdatePayload) and 196-204 (publish overloads) vs src/haute/server.py:644-651 (publishes graph_fingerprint)
claim.failure_scenario: The watcher's default_bus.publish('graph.update', {graph, graph_fingerprint, source_file}) carries a key (graph_fingerprint) that the TypedDict contract does not declare. At runtime _ws_graph_update_subscriber forwards the whole payload (including graph_fingerprint) into the WS frame, so the wire is correct today. But the bus' static contract is misleading: a new subscriber typed against GraphUpdatePayload would see no graph_fingerprint field and a type-checker would flag legitimate access to it (or silently accept a subscriber that drops it). The 'pay for verbosity once for static type-checking at every call site' promise in the module docstring is unmet for this event.
claim.repro_strategy: Static/code-trace: diff the GraphUpdatePayload keys against the dict literal published at server.py:644-651; the missing graph_fingerprint key is the proof. No runtime failure to reproduce; this is a contract-drift design finding.

claim.title: Test-before-live gate scores test quotes WITHOUT bundled artifact_paths, so validate-time loads a different (potentially newer) model than the deployed container serves and skips the contract check
claim.location: src/haute/deploy/_validators.py:375-380 (score_test_quotes -> score_graph, no artifact_paths); src/haute/deploy/_schema.py:134-139 (infer_output_schema -> score_graph, no artifact_paths); contrast src/haute/deploy/_model_code.py:49-57 and src/haute/deploy/_container.py:268-278 which pass artifact_paths; scorer branch src/haute/deploy/_scorer.py:605-704 only engages on remap; base builder src/haute/_builders.py:1152-1209 loads from MLflow run_id/registered_model/version
claim.failure_scenario: A pipeline has a modelScore node with sourceType='registered', registered_model='x', version='latest' (or sourceType='run' whose artifact is later overwritten). `validate_deploy` -> `score_test_quotes` and `infer_output_schema` call `score_graph` with NO artifact_paths. Because the scorer's modelScore intercept only activates when the node is in `remap` (remapped_path/bundled_contract_path both derive from `remap`), it falls through to the base `_build_model_score`, which loads the model live from MLflow using version='latest' AND does not run `_assert_runtime_contract_matches` (no bundled contract is attached). The deploy bundler (`collect_artifacts`) meanwhile downloads and PINS a specific artifact and bundles the feature contract; at serve time pyfunc/container pass `artifact_paths`, so the scorer loads the pinned bytes and DOES enforce the contract. Net: the 'test before live' gate validates against whatever 'latest' resolves to at validate time (or a since-mutated run artifact) and never exercises the actual pinned artifact + contract verification path that ships. Test quotes can pass while the deployed model produces different prices, or a contract drift that would block serving is invisible to validation.
claim.repro_strategy: Build a 2-node graph: apiInput -> modelScore(sourceType='registered', registered_model='m', version='latest'). Register two model versions with different coefficients (or different output dtype). Resolve+validate when 'latest'=v1, then have the bundler pin v1; separately point MLflow 'latest' at v2 and confirm score_test_quotes (no artifact_paths) loads v2 while score_graph(..., artifact_paths=resolved.artifacts) loads v1 — different predictions for the same quote. Minimal: assert score_test_quotes path never invokes _assert_runtime_contract_matches by feeding a contract-mismatching input and observing validation passes but serve-path score_graph(artifact_paths=...) raises FeatureMismatchError.

verdict.repro_outcome: Exit 0 (reproduced). Same apiInput->modelScore(sourceType='run')->output graph + same 1-row input scored two ways. VALIDATE path = score_graph WITHOUT artifact_paths (the exact shape at _validators.py:375-380 / _schema.py:134-139): PASSED, returned prediction 2.444151757243076, logs show 'mlflow_model_loaded ... source_type=run' (loaded live from MLflow, no contract check). SERVE path = score_graph WITH the pinned bundle incl. feature_contract.json (shape at _model_code.py:54 / _container.py:394,407): raised FeatureMismatchError: contract mismatch: feature_types: expected={'age':'Int64','weight':'Int64'}, actual={'age':'Int64','weight':'Float64'}. Same input -> validation accepts what the deployed container blocks. Repro is fully isolated (tempfile mkdtemp for mlruns + .cache/models, cwd chdir into tempdir, restored in finally); git status confirms no src/ or tests/ files touched.
verdict.evidence: CODE TRACE: (1) score_graph_lazy sets `remap = artifact_paths or {}` (_scorer.py:457); with artifact_paths=None remap is empty. (3) modelScore intercept computes `bundled_contract_path = _bundled_contract_path(nid, remap) if remap else None` and `remapped_path = ... if remap else None` (_scorer.py:606-607) -> both None -> both intercept branches (629 remapped_path, 677 bundled_contract_path) skipped -> _intercept returns None (733) -> base _build_model_score (_builders.py:1152). (5) ModelScorer._categorical_levels_for_score returns at _model_scorer.py:1088-1089 when feature_contract_path is None -> NO _assert_runtime_contract_matches. CONTRAST: serve passes artifact_paths (HauteModel.predict _model_code.py:49-57; container _container.py:268-278,394,407) = bundler-pinned download + bundled contract from collect_artifacts (_bundler.py:84-111, which resolves version incl. 'latest' to a concrete artifact at bundle time, downloads, pins, and bundles feature_contract.json) -> intercept fires -> _load_local_model_cached(pinned bytes) + _assert_runtime_contract_matches (_scorer.py:649-655,320-404). verdict.blast_radius: Every deploy whose scoring path contains a configured modelScore node (sourceType='registered' or 'run'). The 'test before live' gate (validate_deploy -> score_test_quotes, and resolve_config -> infer_output_schema) validates a model loaded live from MLflow with version='latest' (mutable, re-resolved at validate time) AND skips the bundled feature-contract verification.
