claim.title: graphRefreshingRef counter can be left >0 (undo/redo and selection-clear silently disabled) when a WS graph_update throws after incrementing the guard but before scheduling its release, or when overlapping applies desync the shared ref against the effect-local increment counter
claim.location: frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocketSync.ts:290-323 (increment graphRefreshingRef & activeSelectionGuardIncrements inside try; release only scheduled in finally via scheduleDelayed), 126-131 (releaseSelectionGuard), 383-398 (unmount cleanup subtracts activeSelectionGuardIncrements); frontend/src/hooks/useGraphCanvasState.ts:117-125 (undo/redo no-op while graphRefreshingRef.current>0)
claim.failure_scenario: In the graph_update handler, graphRefreshingRef.current is incremented (line 290) and the matching release is registered only via scheduleDelayed(releaseSelectionGuard, 150) in the finally (line 322). The increment and the scheduleDelayed are in the same try/finally so a throw is covered — but the release is a TIMER stored in the effect-local delayedTimers set. If the effect re-runs/unmounts (WS reconnect, dependency change) the cleanup clears all delayedTimers (line 386-389) and then subtracts only activeSelectionGuardIncrements once; across rapid reconnects where graphRefreshingRef was bumped by multiple overlapping applies whose release timers are dropped, the shared graphRefreshingRef can settle at a positive value while activeSelectionGuardIncrements has been zeroed — leaving undo/redo permanently no-op (useGraphCanvasState early-returns) and onSelectionChange swallowed, with no error and no user-visible cause.
claim.repro_strategy: Code-trace / integration argument: drive the WS effect through two overlapping graph_update applies (so graphRefreshingRef reaches 2 and activeSelectionGuardIncrements 2) and unmount before the 150ms release timers fire; show the cleanup path can leave graphRefreshingRef.current>0. A fully deterministic standalone repro needs a fake WebSocket + timer control; the counter desync is visible by instrumenting graphRefreshingRef across the lifecycle.

verdict.evidence: Both claimed scenarios fail. Scenario A (throw between increment and release scheduling): the claim itself concedes it is covered — useWebSocketSync.ts lines 290-291 increment, the try at 292 wraps the body, and the finally at 321-323 unconditionally calls scheduleDelayed(releaseSelectionGuard,150) even when setNodesRaw throws. Scenario B (the core claim) misreads the cleanup arithmetic. The claim says cleanup "subtracts only activeSelectionGuardIncrements once"; in reality lines 391-394 compute graphRefreshingRef.current = Math.max(0, graphRefreshingRef.current - activeSelectionGuardIncrements) — it subtracts the FULL accumulated count N in one operation, exactly matching the N dropped release timers. Invariant proof: lines 290-291 are consecutive synchronous statements (no await/branch/return between), so the shared ref D and local counter A always rise in lockstep; releaseSelectionGuard (126-131) decrements both together; grep confirms useWebSocketSync.ts is the ONLY module that WRITES graphRefreshingRef (useGraphCanvasState/useEdgeHandlers only read it), and activeSelectionGuardIncrements is a fresh let per effect run (line 115). Each effect's contribution to D equals its A, and cleanup removes exactly that, so D = max(0, N - N) = 0. EXECUTED: repro drove the claim's exact 2- and 3-overlapping-apply-then-unmount-before-150ms scenario. Intermediate expect(ref).toBe(2)/toBe(3) PASSED (guard genuinely reached the elevated value the claim describes), and post-unmount expect(ref).toBe(0) PASSED. An inverted run asserting toBeGreaterThan(0) FAILED with "AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0" — proving the ref is truly 0, never the stuck-positive state the claim predicts. Existing suites corroborate: useWebSocketSync.gaps.test.ts:528-560 (unmount before 150ms -> ref 0) and useWebSocketSync.failLoudly.test.ts:143-175 (layout throws -> ref restored to 0); 17/17 passed.
verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (claim refuted). Ran a frontend-root copy via a temporary override vitest config (jsdom + setupTests). Both repro tests passed: after 2 (and 3) overlapping graph_update applies the guard reached 2 (and 3) as the claim describes, and after unmounting before the 150ms release timers fired, graphRefreshingRef.current was 0 — NOT the positive value the claim predicts. A deliberately inverted variant (assert >0) failed with "expected 0 to be greater than 0", confirming the ref is genuinely 0. Temp run files were removed afterward; no src/ or tests/ files were modified (git status shows only untracked review/).

claim.title: A parse_error frame arriving during the async dagre layout await does not bump graphUpdateSeq, so an in-flight graph_update for the same file still applies afterward and clears the parse-error banner — leaving the canvas showing a graph the backend has since reported unparseable
claim.location: frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocketSync.ts:259-305 (graph_update: await getLayoutedElements, then re-check only updateSeq!==graphUpdateSeq and dirty, then setSyncBanner(null) at 303), 354-360 (parse_error only sets banner + nulls appliedGraphFingerprintRef; does NOT increment graphUpdateSeq)
claim.failure_scenario: Backend sends graph_update for file F (no positions, so getLayoutedElements runs and the handler awaits). While awaiting, the file is edited again to an unparseable state and the backend sends parse_error for F. The parse_error branch sets the banner ('Parse error...') but does not increment graphUpdateSeq. The awaited graph_update resumes: updateSeq still equals graphUpdateSeq, dirty is still false, so it applies setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw, calls setSyncBanner(null) (line 303) clearing the parse-error banner, and markSaved(). The user is left viewing the now-stale parsed graph as if current, with the unparseable-file warning erased.
claim.repro_strategy: Integration test with a mock WebSocket and a controllable getLayoutedElements promise: deliver graph_update (positions all zero to force layout), then resolve a parse_error frame before resolving the layout promise, then resolve layout. Assert the banner is left null and nodes were replaced — i.e. the graph_update won over the later parse_error.

verdict.evidence: Traced frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocketSync.ts. The graph_update branch is the ONLY place that bumps the sequence: line 254 `const updateSeq = ++graphUpdateSeq`. For a graph parsed from a .py file the nodes have no non-zero positions (positions are a frontend-only concern; backend builds graph via `parse_pipeline_to_graph(...).model_dump()` at server.py:238-239), so `hasPositions` (262-264) is false and the handler takes `nodesToApply = await getLayoutedElements(newNodes, newEdges)` at line 267 — a real async yield (utils/layout.ts:13-20,81-82 dynamic-imports elkjs then awaits elk.layout). After the await the ONLY staleness guard is line 269 `if (!mounted || updateSeq !== graphUpdateSeq) return` and the dirty guard line 272 `if (blockDirtyGraphUpdate(incomingSource)) return`. On success it reaches line 303 `setSyncBanner(null)`. The parse_error branch (lines 354-360) runs `appliedGraphFingerprintRef.current = null` (358) and `setSyncBanner(String(msg.error ...))` (359) but contains NO `++graphUpdateSeq`. Therefore a parse_error frame delivered while graph_update is suspended at the await sets the banner, but does NOT invalidate the in-flight update: on resume updateSeq still equals graphUpdateSeq (269 passes), dirty is still false (272 passes), so setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw apply the now-stale parsed graph and line 303 setSyncBanner(null) erases the parse-error banner, then markSaved() (304). The existing test at useWebSocketSync.gaps.test.ts:393-458 proves the mechanism and harness: a SECOND graph_update (which DOES `++graphUpdateSeq`) correctly drops the stale in-flight one — parse_error lacks exactly this increment, which is the asymmetry being claimed. Reachability is confirmed in src/haute/server.py:514-682 where the file watcher broadcasts graph.update (successful parse, no positions, 644-651) and parse.error (failed parse, 664-667) as independent fire-and-forget tasks (_broadcast_event_as_ws_message -> loop.create_task at line 129); two edits parseable->unparseable produce both frames, the parse_error arriving during the layout await window.
verdict.repro_outcome: Not executed (frontend TS/React claim — per instructions, code-trace proof produced instead of execution). Note the existing vitest at frontend/src/__tests__/hooks/useWebSocketSync.gaps.test.ts already mocks WebSocket + a controllable getLayoutedElements promise (lines 397-458), so the claim's repro_strategy is directly implementable: deliver graph_update with positions {x:0,y:0} to force the layout await, fire parse_error before resolving the layout promise, then resolve layout, and assert setSyncBanner's last value is null and setNodesRaw was called with the stale graph.
verdict.blast_radius: Live file-sync correctness in the visual editor. When a user edits a pipeline .py to a valid state then quickly to an unparseable state (or the file watcher emits graph_update then parse_error close together), the parse-error banner can be silently erased and the canvas left displaying the previously-parsed (now stale) graph as if current, plus markSaved() resets the dirty flag. The user is misled into thinking the backend accepted a file it has actually rejected. Self-heals on the next file event or on reconnect/resync, and requires the specific timing window (parse_error arriving during the layout await), so it is intermittent rather than systematic. No data loss to disk (server is authoritative); the harm is a misleading UI state.
verdict.recommended_fix: Make parse_error participate in the same sequence/versioning used by graph_update so an in-flight graph_update for the same file is invalidated. Simplest: in the parse_error branch (after the isCurrentSourceFile guard, ~line 357) add `++graphUpdateSeq` (the same counter graph_update captures at line 254). Then a parse_error that arrives during the layout await bumps graphUpdateSeq, so the resumed graph_update's `updateSeq !== graphUpdateSeq` check at line 269 fails and it early-returns, leaving the parse-error banner intact. Add a regression test mirroring useWebSocketSync.gaps.test.ts:393-458 but interleaving a parse_error (instead of a second graph_update) during the controllable layout promise, asserting the final syncBanner is the parse-error message and setNodesRaw was NOT called with the stale graph.
verdict.coordinate_risk: High — this exact handler is actively being edited on the in-flight branch wave-2-cache-integrity (git diff main...HEAD shows +169/-13 lines in useWebSocketSync.ts), and commit 8b6dc6fa "Harden W6 live sync work-loss guards" touched the dirty-guard/banner logic in this same graph_update path. The single-line fix and its test should be coordinated with whoever owns the W6 live-sync guards to avoid merge conflicts and to reuse the same sequence-guard pattern.

claim.title: normalizeEdges strips type/animated but never validates that edge.source/target nodes exist or that sourceHandle/targetHandle is a live port; a backend-sent or file-sync'd edge with a missing endpoint or stale handle is admitted, indexed by the cascade/trace, and re-emitted by codegen on the next save
claim.location: frontend/src/utils/graphHelpers.ts:24-26 (normalizeEdges only maps type/animated); consumed at frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineAPI.ts:233 (initial load) and frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocketSync.ts:261 (graph_update); cascade adjacency in usePipelineAPI.ts:337-366; no general endpoint-existence guard (cf. the apiInput-specific reconcileApiInputEdges)
claim.failure_scenario: A pipeline file (or a backend graph_update) contains an edge whose source or target node id is absent from the nodes array, or whose sourceHandle names a port that no longer emits. normalizeEdges passes it through verbatim into the store. The frontend has strong apiInput-specific edge reconciliation but no general 'both endpoints exist' guard on import. The dangling edge participates in the downstream-preview cascade BFS (childrenBySource map) and trace edge adjacency, and on the next handleSave it is captured into the GraphPayload and re-emitted by codegen as a pipeline.connect(...) — which then KeyErrors in the executor when the saved file is run standalone. A graph integrity defect round-trips silently from file to disk.
claim.repro_strategy: Unit test: normalizeEdges([{id:'e1', source:'missing', target:'n1'}]) returns the edge unchanged (no drop, no throw). Then with nodes=[{id:'n1'}], show captureGraphSnapshot/savePipeline payload still contains edge e1 referencing the non-existent 'missing' node.

verdict.evidence: normalizeEdges (graphHelpers.ts:24-26) only rewrites type/animated: `edges.map((e) => ({ ...e, type: "default", animated: false }))` — no endpoint/handle validation. Consumed at usePipelineAPI.ts:233 and useWebSocketSync.ts:261. The load-boundary guard parsePipelineResponse (guards.ts:604-619) only does expectArray on edges. An EXISTING passing test (resilience.test.ts:757) asserts "normalizeEdges does not validate node existence — passes through orphan edges", and :769 "buildGraph includes orphan edges (validation is server-side)". Cascade BFS (usePipelineAPI.ts:337-344) indexes childrenBySource from raw edges with no endpoint check. reconcileApiInputEdges (apiInputPorts.ts:231-259) only prunes edges where edge.source===nodeId against that apiInput's config ports — apiInput-source-specific, never a general "both endpoints exist" guard. Round-trip: savePipeline (client.ts:517-530) posts the graph verbatim; SavePipelineService.save validations have no endpoint check; flatten_graph returns unchanged when no submodels (_flatten.py:24-25); validate_pipeline_graph_shape_contracts (_graph_shape.py:65-87, lines 24-28) silently ignores unknown-endpoint edges; topo_sort_ids (_topo.py:60-64) "silently skips" them; graph_to_code connect_pairs (codegen.py:937-945) emits pipeline.connect for EVERY edge via `id_to_func.get(e.source, e.source)` → `pipeline.connect("missing", "n1")`. Pipeline.connect (pipeline.py:235-238) then raises `ValueError("Source node 'missing' not found in pipeline...")` when the saved standalone file is imported/run. Every link in the claimed chain is confirmed.
verdict.repro_outcome: No script executed. This is a frontend-rooted claim whose round-trip spans React/zustand store + FastAPI save + codegen and cannot be cleanly isolated; the load-time admission is already proven by an existing passing unit test (resilience.test.ts:757/:769). Backend codegen re-emission and the standalone-run ValueError are proven by direct line trace (codegen.py:937-945, pipeline.py:235-238).
verdict.blast_radius: A pipeline file or backend graph_update containing an edge with a missing source/target node id (or a stale sourceHandle no longer emitted) is admitted by normalizeEdges, indexed by the cascade/trace adjacency, preserved through captureGraphSnapshot, and re-emitted by codegen on the next save as pipeline.connect("<missing>", ...). The saved standalone .py then raises ValueError at module build time when run outside the editor. Trigger requires an externally-malformed input — normal editor interaction maintains referential integrity (React Flow + apiInput reconciliation), so it is not reachable by ordinary GUI use. Per repo convention (CLAUDE.md), start with a failing test: normalizeEdges([{id:'e1',source:'missing',target:'n1'}]) with nodes=[{id:'n1'}] must drop e1 (and a save-payload test asserting the GraphPayload no longer contains e1).
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. Current branch is wave-2-cache-integrity and the claim's region (frontend graph import/edge handling, codegen edge emission) is graph-integrity-adjacent; an in-flight cache/integrity wave could be editing useGraphStore / usePipelineAPI / codegen. graphHelpers.ts and apiInputPorts.ts themselves look stable. claim.title: isCurrentSourceFile treats an absolute path and a relative path as the same file by pure suffix match (endsWith('/'+relative)) and returns true whenever either side is blank/unnormalizable; a relative source that is a directory-suffix of an unrelated absolute path passes, applying an external graph_update to the wrong open pipeline
claim.location: frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocketSync.ts:63-82 (isCurrentSourceFile / isAbsoluteRelativeMatch using absolute.endsWith('/'+relative)), 251-257 (gate for graph_update), 355 (gate for parse_error)
claim.failure_scenario: Open pipeline source is the relative 'models/pricing.py'. The backend emits a graph_update whose source_file is an absolute path that merely ends with '/models/pricing.py' but lives under a different project root (e.g. '/other/repo/models/pricing.py'). isAbsoluteRelativeMatch returns true on the suffix, so the update is accepted and (when the local graph is not dirty) the open graph is replaced with the other file's nodes/edges/preamble, then markSaved() makes it look clean. Also, when either source normalizes to blank (line 71) the function returns true unconditionally, accepting any update. This is a file-identity confusion across the file-sync trust boundary that can silently swap the user's open pipeline for a different file's content.
claim.repro_strategy: Pure-function unit test: isCurrentSourceFile('/other/repo/models/pricing.py', 'models/pricing.py') === true (suffix collision across unrelated roots), and isCurrentSourceFile('', 'models/pricing.py') === true (blank-side passthrough). Both demonstrate accepting an update that should be rejected.

verdict.evidence:
Traced isCurrentSourceFile (frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocketSync.ts:68-82) and its helpers for both asserted cases. Both pure-function claims hold:

CASE A — isCurrentSourceFile('/other/repo/models/pricing.py', 'models/pricing.py'):
- L69 incomingSource='/other/repo/models/pricing.py'; L70 currentSource='models/pricing.py' (both non-null, L71 not taken).
- L72 not equal; L73 incomingIsAbsolute=true (startsWith '/'); L74 currentIsAbsolute=false.
- L75 branch taken -> L76 isAbsoluteRelativeMatch(abs, rel): L64 hasDirectorySegment('models/pricing.py')=true; L65 '/other/repo/models/pricing.py'.endsWith('/models/pricing.py')=TRUE. => returns true. Suffix collision across unrelated roots confirmed.

CASE B — isCurrentSourceFile('', 'models/pricing.py'):
- L69 normalizeSourceFile('') -> trim '' -> returns null (L48). L71 `if (!incomingSource || !currentSource) return true` -> returns TRUE unconditionally. Fail-open blank passthrough confirmed.

These two are the exact gate used at L251 (graph_update) and L355 (parse_error). On the clean-graph happy path the update is applied and markSaved() runs (L293-304); blockDirtyGraphUpdate only guards when the store is dirty (L255/L272). endsWith('/'+relative) is a suffix test, not a same-file identity test, and the dual-null default fails open — both are genuine correctness defects.
verdict.repro_outcome: Not executed (TS/React claim per instructions). Pure-function assertions proven by exact-line code-trace; both return true as the claim states.
verdict.blast_radius: The unsound identity check gates every graph_update/parse_error applied to the open pipeline. Pure-function defects are real and trace-proven. End-to-end "wrong-file swap" reachability is narrow, though: the backend wire id (_wire_source_file in src/haute/server.py:178-184) is project-relative for in-root pipelines and absolute ONLY for out-of-root files, and sourceFileRef mirrors the last backend value (relative for the normal single-root case). So the absolute-vs-relative branch (L75-79) only fires when an out-of-root pipeline's absolute path tail-collides with the open in-root relative id — an atypical multi-root/symlinked-watch configuration. No graph_update producer emits a blank source_file, so Case B's fail-open default is latent (only a self-directed resync parse_error carries source_file=''). Within one root, each physical file maps to one wire id, so same-root collisions cannot occur. Net: genuine logic weakness, low practical exposure on standard single-root setups.
verdict.recommended_fix: Replace fail-open identity logic with fail-closed, sound matching: (1) When both incoming and current normalize to null/blank, return false (or treat unknown-incoming explicitly) instead of true; require a positive match to accept an external update. (2) For the absolute-vs-relative case, do not accept a bare endsWith suffix: require the absolute path, after stripping a known project-root prefix, to equal the relative id exactly (anchor on a path boundary AND validate against the server's project root rather than any '/'+relative suffix). If the project root is not available client-side, prefer rejecting cross-form mismatches and rely on the backend already emitting a canonical relative id. Add unit tests asserting isCurrentSourceFile('/other/repo/models/pricing.py','models/pricing.py')===false and isCurrentSourceFile('','models/pricing.py')===false, plus the legitimate-match cases that must stay true.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. This file (useWebSocketSync.ts) and the source_file sync/trust boundary are squarely in the cache-integrity wave area (current branch wave-2-cache-integrity; appliedGraphFingerprintRef / resync fingerprinting was recently added here). An in-flight branch may be editing the same gate, so a fix should be coordinated to avoid conflicts with fingerprint-resync changes.

claim.title: hashConfig uses 32-bit djb2 over JSON.stringify(sortKeys(config)) for solve/train/explore staleness and estimate-staleness; a hash collision between two materially different configs makes a config change read as 'not stale', showing an outdated solve/train/explore result (and stale config-changed banner) as current
claim.location: frontend/src/stores/useNodeResultsStore.ts:167-187 (djb2 + hashConfig); configHash compared for staleness in ExplorePreview.tsx:83-94 and the solve/train CachedSolveResult.configHash / CachedTrainResult.configHash paths (useNodeResultsStore.ts:717-727, 938-943)
claim.failure_scenario: Solve/train/explore result freshness is gated on equality of a 32-bit djb2 digest of the canonicalized config. djb2 over a 4-byte space has ~1-in-4e9 collision per pair, but the staleness check is a single equality between the last-run hash and the current hash. If a user edits the optimiser/model config to a different config whose djb2 happens to equal the previous config's, the panel treats the displayed result as still matching the current config (no 'config changed since last run' indication) and the actuary acts on an optimisation/training result computed for a DIFFERENT config. The cost of a wrong rate is high relative to the (low but nonzero) collision probability, and a full canonical-string compare (already available via the graphSnapshot canonicalize) would be exact.
claim.repro_strategy: Property/brute test: search small synthetic config dicts for two whose hashConfig() outputs collide (djb2 32-bit makes a collision findable by enumerating numeric tweaks), then show ExplorePreview's currentCachedResult logic (configHash equality) treats the post-edit config as matching the pre-edit cached result. Even without finding a natural collision, a unit test can monkeypatch two configs to the same djb2 to demonstrate the staleness-miss path.

verdict.repro_outcome: PASS (bug demonstrated). Ran `node review/02-findings/repro/frontend__hashconfig-djb2-32bit-collision-staleness.mjs`. In 0.6s it found two materially different configs (differing only in a user-editable `label` field) with identical hashConfig() digest `jldciw`: canonical A != canonical B (true) yet digests equal (true). Applying the exact UI staleness predicate (useStaleConfigEstimate.ts:60 `cachedConfigHash !== currentConfigHash`) returned isStale=false (SHOULD be true), and the ExplorePreview.tsx:92 predicate (`cachedResult.configHash === currentConfigHash`) returned the stale cached result (RESULT_FOR_CONFIG_A) as current while the live config is B. djb2 + hashConfig were ported verbatim from useNodeResultsStore.ts lines 168-187. The mjs port is a faithful copy of the pure TS function; no project src/tests touched.
verdict.evidence: Code-trace + executed repro agree. (1) 32-bit digest: useNodeResultsStore.ts:173 `return (hash >>> 0).toString(36)` — uint32 codomain; hashConfig:186 `return djb2(JSON.stringify(sortKeys(rest)))` returns ONLY the digest (canonical string discarded). (2) Staleness is a single equality of that digest in every path: ExplorePreview.tsx:92 `cachedResult && cachedResult.configHash === configHash && cachedResult.source === activeSource` (structuralVersion is stored on the cached explore result at useNodeResultsStore.ts:1038 but NOT compared here; source is partly redundant — folded into the hash at ExplorePreview.tsx:84); useStaleConfigEstimate.ts:60 `const isStale = !!cachedResult && cachedResult.configHash !== configHash`, surfaced as the suppressible 'config changed' banner at OptimiserConfig.tsx:1050 `{isStale && (<div ...RefreshCw...)}`; cached solve/train results persist the same digest (useNodeResultsStore.ts:722 `configHash: job.configHash`, :942 `configHash: job?.configHash ?? ""`). (3) No exact-compare guard exists. (4) Repro output: `hashConfig(A) = jldciw`, `hashConfig(B) = jldciw`, `UI reports stale? false (SHOULD be true)`, `ExplorePreview serves cached result for config A as current? true`. (5) An exact alternative is genuinely available: graphSnapshot.ts already provides deterministic `canonicalize` (lines 78-88) + full-string compare via serializeSnapshot/selectIsDirty for dirty-tracking. Calibration: the mechanism is exactly as claimed, but realistic per-edit collision probability is ~1/2^32 (~2.3e-10) since each check compares the current hash against a SINGLE prior hash (no birthday amplification in production); the repro hit a collision quickly only by enumerating tens of thousands of synthetic configs, which a real user never does.
verdict.blast_radius: All three between-run staleness judgements in the visual editor: ExplorePreview currentCachedResult/currentExploreJob freshness (panels/ExplorePreview.tsx:87-94), OptimiserConfig solve-staleness banner (panels/OptimiserConfig.tsx:1050 via hooks/useStaleConfigEstimate.ts:60), and ModellingConfig train-staleness (panels/ModellingConfig.tsx via the same hook). On a digest collision a config change reads as 'not stale': the config-changed banner is suppressed and an outdated solve/train/explore result is shown as matching the current config, so an actuary could act on an optimisation/training result computed for a different config. Backend cannot mask it — the judgement is purely frontend and happens before any re-run. Realistic occurrence is vanishingly rare (single-pair equality, ~1/2^32 per edit).
verdict.recommended_fix: Make the staleness key exact instead of a 32-bit digest. Either (a) store and compare the canonical config string directly (the existing canonicalize/serializeSnapshot pattern in utils/graphSnapshot.ts gives a deterministic, key-order-stable serialization to reuse) — `cachedResult.configKey !== currentConfigKey` is then exact; or (b) if a fixed-width digest is wanted for memory, widen to a 128-bit hash and keep equality. Keep hashConfig's existing internal-key stripping (_nodeId/_columns/_schemaWarnings/_availableColumns). Add a unit test asserting that two configs which differ only in one field are always treated as stale (and a regression test that forces equal digests via monkeypatch to prove an exact compare still flags staleness).
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate — this is the cache-integrity hot zone and the current branch is `wave-2-cache-integrity`. useNodeResultsStore.ts plus ExplorePreview/OptimiserConfig/ModellingConfig staleness paths are exactly the kind of code an in-flight cache-integrity wave is likely editing, so a fix here may overlap/conflict with concurrent work on the same files. The change itself is localized (hashConfig + the three equality sites) and low-API-surface.

claim.title: WS graph_update layout decision uses a graph-wide hasPositions flag (any single node not at origin); a backend graph containing a legitimately origin-placed node, or a newly added node defaulting to (0,0), is left at the origin (overlapping) because the presence of any other non-origin node suppresses the dagre auto-layout for the whole graph
claim.location: frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocketSync.ts:262-267 (hasPositions = newNodes.some(n=>x!==0||y!==0); nodesToApply = hasPositions ? newNodes : await getLayoutedElements(...))
claim.failure_scenario: On a graph_update, if ANY node has a non-origin position the code applies all incoming positions verbatim and skips dagre. A pipeline where one node is intentionally (or incidentally) at (0,0) — or where the backend round-trips a new node without a position so it defaults to (0,0) while existing nodes carry positions — renders that node stacked at the canvas origin on top of whatever else is there, with no per-node layout fallback. The heuristic is all-or-nothing across the graph rather than per-node, so partial-position graphs are mislaid.
claim.repro_strategy: Unit test the layout decision in isolation: given newNodes = [{id:'a',position:{x:100,y:50}},{id:'b',position:{x:0,y:0}}], assert hasPositions===true so getLayoutedElements is NOT called and node 'b' stays at (0,0). Demonstrates the graph-wide gate leaving an origin node unlaid-out.

verdict.blast_radius: Visual editor only (React/TS). Affects a graph_update (file-watcher reparse or reconnect resync) where the incoming graph mixes origin-defaulted nodes with non-origin nodes. The pipeline data/codegen is unaffected; only canvas placement of the origin-defaulted node(s) is wrong until the user drags them or triggers a full re-layout. No data loss, no backend correctness impact.
verdict.recommended_fix: Make the layout decision per-node instead of graph-wide. Keep verbatim positions for nodes whose position is meaningful (non-origin OR present in the sidecar), and run getLayoutedElements only for the subset lacking a real position — feeding the already-known positions in as fixed/anchor constraints so ELK places the new nodes relative to the existing layout. Minimal alternative: detect nodes at (0,0) that have no sidecar entry and route just those through layout. Add a frontend unit test asserting that newNodes=[{a:(100,50)},{b:(0,0)}] results in node b being repositioned (not left at origin), and a backend test that parse_pipeline_to_graph leaves a new (un-sidecarred) node at its default while sidecar nodes keep custom positions, so the partial-position contract is pinned.
verdict.coordinate_risk: Moderate. useWebSocketSync.ts is a hot file on the in-flight branch wave-2-cache-integrity (~169 insertions vs main), so a fix here is likely to conflict with concurrent edits to this exact hook. The hasPositions gate itself predates those edits. The fix also straddles frontend (layout.ts / the hook) and a backend invariant (parse_pipeline_to_graph sidecar merge), so coordinate with whoever owns the live-sync work.
verdict.evidence: Verbatim gate at frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocketSync.ts:262-267: `const hasPositions = newNodes.some((n: Node) => n.position && (n.position.x !== 0 || n.position.y !== 0)); const nodesToApply = hasPositions ? newNodes : await getLayoutedElements(newNodes, newEdges)`. some() is graph-wide, so ANY non-origin node makes ALL incoming positions applied verbatim and skips ELK (getLayoutedElements in utils/layout.ts relays out the whole graph; no per-node fallback). Partial-position graphs genuinely reach this code: src/haute/_graph_builders.py:166-181 `_build_rf_nodes` sets position={"x": i*x_spacing, "y": 0} (index 0 -> exactly (0,0)); src/haute/routes/_helpers.py:733-736 `parse_pipeline_to_graph` overrides position ONLY when positions.get(node.id) is not None, so a newly added node with no .haute.json sidecar entry keeps its (0,0) default while previously-dragged nodes get non-origin sidecar positions. That graph is emitted via graph.model_dump() over the WS graph_update frame at server.py:634-651 (file watcher) and server.py:226-249 (resync); GraphNode.position (_types.py:607) serializes as {"x":float,"y":float} numbers, matching the frontend's !==0 check. The existing test "uses layout when nodes have no positions" only covers the all-origin case (single node at 0,0); no test covers the partial case, and "updates nodes and edges on graph_update with positions" confirms positioned nodes are applied verbatim. The repro_strategy assertion holds exactly: for newNodes=[{a:(100,50)},{b:(0,0)}], some() is true via a, getLayoutedElements is NOT called, and b is applied at (0,0). Nuance: the claim's "overlapping/stacked on top of whatever else is there" is only guaranteed when another node also lands at/near origin; the always-true defect is an origin-stranded node left without auto-layout despite a positioned graph (consistent with claimed severity: low).
verdict.repro_outcome: No script executed: per instructions, frontend (TS/React) claims are proven by definitive code-trace rather than a Python repro (the data path runs through React Flow + WebSocket, not importable haute Python state). Control/data flow traced end-to-end above establishes the wrong behaviour.
